Santé de la reproduction et migration interne : l’AJSPD lance l’édition 2026 de son Prix
items.description: L'Association des Journalistes en Santé, Population et Développement (AJSPD) a lancé officiellement l'édition 2026 de son prix annuel, consacrée cette année à la « santé de la reproduction et migration interne ». L'initiative est menée en partenariat avec l'African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC). Après l'édition 2025 centrée sur la malnutrition infantile, l'association veut cette fois attirer l'attention sur la situation sanitaire des populations mobiles au Sénégal. Selon l'AJSPD, les déplacements de jeunes et de femmes des zones rurales vers les centres urbains, mais aussi en provenance de pays frontaliers, créent de nouvelles vulnérabilités : accès limité aux soins de santé sexuelle et reproductive, risques de grossesses non désirées, précarité sociale et inégalités de genre. Les journalistes candidats sont invités à produire des reportages sur l'accès des jeunes migrants aux services de santé reproductive, ainsi que sur la contraception et la planification familiale dans les zones d'accueil. L'association souligne le rôle des professionnels des médias pour traduire les données scientifiques en messages accessibles aux communautés. L'appel à candidatures, lancé le 2 octobre, sera suivi d'un webinaire de renforcement des capacités, animé par des experts et des chercheurs. La production et la soumission des travaux, ainsi que leur évaluation par un jury indépendant, se dérouleront durant le mois de novembre. La cérémonie nationale de remise des prix est fixée au 5 décembre 2026. Les catégories récompensées Le prix distinguera les meilleures productions en presse écrite, presse en ligne, radio et télévision. Un Prix Jeune Journaliste, réservé aux moins de 35 ans, et un Grand Prix du Journalisme en Santé, qui couronnera la meilleure production toutes catégories confondues, seront également décernés. Au maximum deux prix seront attribués par catégorie. Les dossiers seront jugés sur la rigueur factuelle, l'usage pertinent des données scientifiques, la qualité narrative, le respect de l'éthique et de la déontologie, ainsi que leur impact potentiel sur la sensibilisation du public. Dans le communiqué, le président de l'AJSPD, Eugène Kaly, rappelle l'engagement de l'association pour une information sanitaire fiable, rigoureuse et accessible, afin d'améliorer les comportements de santé et de renforcer la redevabilité des systèmes de santé au Sénégal.

items.title: Collapsed towers disrupt power supply in Nasarawa
items.description: ABUJA — The Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) has announced the unavailability of all 33kV outgoing feeders at the Keffi and Akwanga transmission substations in Nasarawa State following the collapse of three transmission towers. The affected towers — T78, T79 and T80 — are located along the Karu-Keffi-Akwanga 132kV transmission line corridor. TCN disclosed this in a statement posted on its X platform on Thursday, saying the incident occurred at about 4:06pm on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, during rainy and windy conditions. According to the company, the 132kV Karu-Keffi-Akwanga Single Circuit Transmission Line tripped on overcurrent relay protection during the incident. “Investigations revealed that three transmission towers have collapsed. TCN promptly isolated for safety,” the statement said. The company said the collapse had rendered all 33kV outgoing feeders at the 132/33kV Keffi and 132/33kV Akwanga transmission substations unavailable. It added that no load could be nominated on the affected feeders until further notice. TCN said its engineers were already at the site to assess the extent of the damage and determine the materials and other requirements needed to commence restoration work. The company apologised to electricity consumers supplied from the affected substations for the disruption. “Please bear with us as we make every effort to ensure that necessary repairs are completed as quickly as possible to enable the restoration of bulk power supply,” it said. TCN assured the public that it would continue to provide updates as restoration efforts progressed. The post Collapsed towers disrupt power supply in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lakurawa attack kills two soldiers, Chinese national in Kebbi
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi BIRNIN KEBBI — Suspected Lakurawa terrorists have killed two soldiers and a Chinese national in an attack on construction workers in Maiyama Local Government Area of Kebbi State. The attackers reportedly infiltrated the area from Kebbe Local Government Area of neighbouring Sokoto State and launched a surprise attack on the workers on Thursday. The spokesperson for the Kebbi State Police Command, SP Bashir Usman, confirmed the attack in a telephone interview. Usman said the victims were among construction workers engaged on the Badagry Super Highway project in Kebbi State, adding that the two soldiers were providing security for the Chinese national and other workers when the attackers struck. He said the attackers killed two soldiers and the Chinese national, while some other people sustained injuries. “Yes, the attack occurred, but the terrorists are not from Kebbi State but infiltrated the state through a village with a border to Kebbi State,” Usman said. He explained that the identities of the deceased soldiers could not be disclosed because they were military personnel and not members of the police. The police spokesperson described the attack as barbaric and unwarranted, adding that joint security agencies had launched a manhunt for the suspected attackers. He said security operatives were pursuing the suspected Lakurawa members responsible for the attack. Lakurawa, a relatively new armed group reported to be operating around parts of north-western Nigeria and the Niger Republic border area, has previously been linked to attacks in the region. items.title: FBI arrests 130 over Ghana scam-centre operation
items.description: WASHINGTON — The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced the arrest and detention of more than 130 people in Ghana in a crackdown on an alleged international scam-centre network targeting American citizens. FBI Director Kash Patel disclosed this on his X platform on Thursday while providing an update on what he described as “Operation Blackout”, a global campaign against scam centres. According to Patel, the latest operation in Ghana has so far identified nearly $10 million in losses involving 89 victims, while more than 300 devices were seized. He said more than 130 individuals had been arrested or detained, including people identified as victims who would be repatriated to their home countries. “Another takedown this week out of Ghana,” Patel said, adding that the investigation was ongoing. He said the alleged scam compounds targeted American citizens and described the operation as part of the FBI’s broader efforts to disrupt such networks around the world. Patel also gave an update on the cumulative results of Operation Blackout, saying about $17 billion had been seized since the campaign began. He said the operation had also resulted in the arrest of hundreds of alleged scammers and the rescue of thousands of trafficked workers. According to the FBI director, more than 10,000 Americans had been warned before losing their money, while an estimated $670 million in losses had been prevented. Patel said the investigation into the latest operation was continuing, promising that more details would be released. The post FBI arrests 130 over Ghana scam-centre operation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Three sisters drowned in sea in joint suicide – UK coroner
items.description: Three British sisters who drowned in the sea in southern England in May died by suicide, a coroner ruled on Thursday at an inquest. The women’s bodies were pulled from the sea at Brighton in the early hours of May 13 in windy weather. Coroner Penelope Schofield concluded the women — 36-year-old Jane Adetoro, 32-year-old Christina Walters and 31-year-old Rebecca Walters — had intended to end their lives. The women arrived in the city late in the evening by pre-booked taxi from London and were last seen alive on the beach around 3:00 am. They entered the water in the dark when “sea conditions were adverse” but “they could not swim”, the coroner said. The coroner said the women “lived very secluded lives”, adding: “We don’t know why they took this course of action or indeed why they chose to do it in Brighton.” A day earlier, the three sisters, who shared a flat in London, had travelled to visit the area where their mother had drowned herself in a lake 16 years earlier, the court heard. Police said earlier there was no evidence of criminality and the women had not visited any local businesses or nightclubs. The post Three sisters drowned in sea in joint suicide – UK coroner appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: États-Unis : Trump refuse d’inviter les observateurs de l’OSCE aux élections de mi-mandat, une première depuis 2002
items.description: L'administration Trump a decide de ne pas inviter de mission de l'Organisation pour la securite et la cooperation en Europe (OSCE) a observer les elections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre. Depuis 2002, l'organisation avait suivi douze scrutins federaux americains, dont six elections de mi-mandat. Ses representants avaient notamment ete accueillis en 2018, sous la premiere presidence de Donald Trump. Ces missions examinent le deroulement des elections et publient leurs conclusions, sans pouvoir intervenir dans les operations de vote ni annuler les resultats. Le departement d'etat justifie ce refus en estimant que l'OSCE devrait consacrer ses ressources limitees aux elections ou son action serait la plus utile. L'organisation a toutefois qualifie cette decision de « regrettable » et estime qu'elle ne respectait pas les engagements de Washington. Parallelement, les etats-Unis envisagent de deployer environ 1 000 observateurs du ministere de la Justice dans les bureaux de vote. Cette initiative suscite des inquietudes concernant les droits des electeurs, alors que la mission internationale de l'OSCE n'a pas ete invitee. Ce refus met en lumiere un changement de position americain. En 2024, le departement d'etat critiquait la Russie pour une cooperation avec l'OSCE qu'il jugeait insuffisante, tout en defendant l'impartialite de ses observateurs. Deux ans plus tard, Washington renonce lui-meme a les inviter a ses elections federales. Un scrutin qui pourrait affaiblir Donald Trump Cette decision intervient a moins d'un mois d'elections decisives pour le controle du Congres. Le 3 novembre, les Americains renouvelleront les 435 sieges de la Chambre des representants et une partie du Senat. Les republicains risquent de perdre leur majorite dans une ou dans les deux chambres. Les intentions de vote nationales placent actuellement les democrates en tete, avec 51,3 % contre 41,6 % pour les republicains. Les projections electorales leur attribuent egalement 93 % de chances de remporter la Chambre des representants et 74 % de conquerir le Senat. Ces estimations restent neanmoins susceptibles d'evoluer avant le vote. Une victoire democrate pourrait reduire considerablement la marge de manœuvre de Donald Trump. Le president americain serait alors contraint de composer avec une opposition renforcee au Congres pour faire adopter une partie de son programme. La guerre contre l'Iran accentue les difficultes de Washington La campagne se deroule egalement dans un contexte de forte opposition a la guerre contre l'Iran. Selon les sondages, 60 % des Americains desapprouvent le conflit, contre 32,1 % qui le soutiennent. Les preoccupations economiques, notamment le niveau eleve des prix des carburants, s'ajoutent aux difficultes rencontrees par l'administration americaine. Malgre l'impopularite du conflit, Washington etudie la possibilite de nouvelles operations militaires d'envergure contre l'Iran , eventuellement avant les elections du 3 novembre. Plusieurs scenarios seraient envisages, sans qu'aucune decision definitive ait ete prise. a l'approche du scrutin, Donald Trump doit ainsi faire face a une possible perte de controle du Congres, tandis que les perspectives d'une nouvelle escalade militaire au Moyen-Orient entretiennent les incertitudes sur la politique americaine.

items.title: Les centres de données vont-ils impacter les midterms ?
items.description: Selon une enquête de l'université Quinnipiac, trois quarts (73 %) d’Américains disent être inquiets quant au fait que les futurs systèmes d’IA pourraient « potentiellement menacer la survie de l’humanité » The Age Of Artificial Intelligence : 73 % Concerned About Potential Threat To Human Survival, Quinnipiac University Poll On AI Finds ; 86 % Support Independent Safety Standards For AI Companies , Quinnipiac Poll, 30 septembre 2026.'> 1 . Cette inquiétude se reflète toutefois encore peu dans les choix des électeurs pour les élections nationales et locales : l’IA est toujours loin derrière le coût de la vie, la corruption, le marché de l’emploi et l’économie. Selon Echelon Insights, seulement 8 % des électeurs citent l’IA comme premier ou deuxième problème majeur auquel le pays est confronté Friday Findings : Will AI produce self-driving cars, bioweapons, or even both ? », The Echelon Review, 25 septembre 2026.'> 2 . Ainsi, malgré la place grandissante qu’occupent les questions de sécurité de l’IA dans le débat public – notamment suite aux incidents survenus ces derniers mois au cours desquels des modèles d’IA ont piraté des sites web – les questions liées au développement de la technologie ne devraient pas jouent un rôle clef dans les élections au Congrès. Selon Jasmine Sun, elles pourraient toutefois peser sur les scrutins locaux Notes on AI & popular politics », 7 octobre 2026.'> 3 . Interconnected Capital recense 321 moratoires sur la construction de centres de données actifs au 8 octobre – soit cinq fois plus qu’il y a cinq mois. Ces derniers, qui couvrent 39 États, sont particulièrement concentrés dans le midwest, comme dans le Michigan, où la question de leur construction a été abordée mardi 6 octobre dans le cadre d'un débat de la campagne électorale pour le poste de gouverneur Michigan gubernatorial candidates clash over data centers ahead of midterm election », CBS News , 7 octobre 2026.'> 4 . Si, selon le Pew Research Center, les démocrates sont plus nombreux que les républicains à affirmer que l’utilisation croissante de l’IA les rend plus inquiets qu’enthousiastes, les campagnes des candidats pour les élections de mi-mandat montrent une critique quasi unanime des centres de données, quelle que soit l’affiliation partisane. Ainsi, sur les 685 campagnes étudiées par Absecon Group, 96 % de celles menées par des candidats démocrates critiquent les centres de données, contre 91 % chez les républicains Absecon Group Report : Over 700 Candidates Are Running Ads Mentioning Data Centers , 8 septembre 2026.'> 5 . Une faible part (10 sur 685, dont 7 républicaines et 3 non-partisanes) adopte une position favorable aux centres de données. L’article Les centres de données vont-ils impacter les midterms ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: COP31 must deliver action, not more promises – African climate negotiators
items.description: The Chair of the African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN), Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, has issued a strong call for global climate talks to move from pledges to tangible action, declaring that COP31 in Antalya must be defined by delivery rather than another cycle of unfulfilled promises. Speaking at the African Group of Negotiators Expert Support (AGNES) Pre-COP31 Strategy Meeting in Nairobi, Dr. Amoah stressed that the global climate process faces a critical test of legitimacy. He warned that the credibility of international negotiations now hinges on a singular question: whether the system can actually deliver implementation on the ground. Highlighting Africa’s core priorities across adaptation, agriculture, loss and damage, climate finance, and just transition, the AGN Chair emphasized that the continent’s demands are fundamental conditions for sustainable development. “When Africa speaks about adaptation, agriculture, finance, loss and damage, just transition and means of implementation, we are not presenting a list of negotiating preferences,” Dr. Amoah asserted. “We are rather talking about the conditions under which our countries can develop, protect their people and build resilient economies in a changing climate.” Addressing the financial architecture, Dr. Amoah called for predictable, scalable, grant-based climate finance for adaptation, rejecting any framing of climate support as international charity. “Africa is not asking for charity,” he declared. “We are asking for an international financial architecture capable of responding fairly to a global problem for which responsibility and vulnerability are profoundly unequal.” He further insisted that the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage must be adequately resourced, responsive, and direct support where it is needed most. “Success cannot be measured by the existence of institutions alone,” Dr. Amoah added. “It must ultimately be measured by whether support reaches countries and communities confronting losses they did little to cause.” On energy policy and industrial strategy, Dr. Amoah warned against uniform transition frameworks that ignore regional economic realities. He stressed that a just transition for Africa must prioritize energy access, clean cooking, poverty eradication, and green industrialization. “Africa cannot simply export raw materials required for the global transition while importing finished technologies at significantly higher value,” Dr. Amoah stated. “The transition must create value in Africa, build industries in Africa, strengthen skills in Africa, and create jobs for Africans. That is part of climate justice too.” He also cautioned negotiators to scrutinize emerging global trade policies, insisting that climate measures must not become a new basis for economic protectionism or inequitable economic relationships. Dr. Amoah outlined a strategic continuum connecting major climate milestones—which he framed as “B2A2A” (Belém to Antalya to Addis Ababa). Under this roadmap, outcomes secured at COP31 in Antalya must establish a firm technical and political foundation for COP32, scheduled to take place in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 2027. He stressed that strong political positioning requires rigorous African technical evidence, praising AGNES for bridging the gap between scientific research and diplomatic negotiations. “At COP31, Africa must not simply be present at the table,” Dr. Amoah concluded. “Africa must help shape what comes out of the room.”

items.title: What happens when you have too little body fat
items.description: From releasing hormones to regulating our temperature, fat has myriad roles in the body. Here’s why chasing extreme fat-loss goals is so unhealthy. Fat has been somewhat demonised for years. Diet culture tells us to burn it, some food companies market low-fat products to us, and weightlifting forums share tips on how to reach as little body fat as possible. You only need to spend a moment scrolling through social media, and you’ll soon find advice on how to “get shredded”. This sinewy physique is defined by extremely well-defined muscles. This year, experts are concerned that the trend to be super skinny is once again resurfacing, in some cases fuelled by the popularity of weight-loss drugs. Yet while too much fat poses health concerns and can lead to obesity, too little is not good for us either. The goal of ridding ourselves of fat can be damaging biologically as well as socially, numerous experts have told me. “We have to love our fat,” Elif Oral, an endocrinologist and professor of medicine at the University of Michigan, tells me. “It plays such an important biological function.” So how much do we really need? And why is too little body fat bad for us? Why body fat matters Broadly speaking, there are two different types of fat: dietary fat and body fat. Dietary fat is the fat you eat in your food, while body fat is nature’s way of storing energy you don’t need. When you eat a meal, the dietary fats, carbohydrates, and proteins in the food are broken down into simple building blocks your body can use for fuel. Carbohydrates become glucose, proteins become amino acids and fats become fatty acids. If you consistently eat more calories than you consume, fat cells – known as adipocytes – store these excess nutrients as lipids. This causes the fat cells to expand in size. However rather than just sitting there passively, we now know that body fat is an active organ which regulates the body’s functions. Just like in the story of Goldilocks and the three bears, our body works best when things are “just right”. Too little, just like too much, is dangerous for our health. We can think of our body fat as a specialised storage vault, taking up nutrients when energy is abundant and releasing them only when needed, says Mikael Ryden, professor of clinical and experimental fat tissue research at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden. It’s a system that helped our ancestors survive periods of food scarcity. Another important role is communication. Fat cells produce hormones that tell the rest of the body how much energy we have and how full we are. The best studied of these is leptin, explains Oral. “Leptin tells the brain there is sufficient energy storage, and then the brain can almost relax,” she says, which leaves the body able to focus on important biological processes such as reproduction and fighting infection. Without leptin, the brain starts to worry about the amount of energy available, meaning essential functions start to be deprioritised. Body fat is also important for staying warm. While white fat stores excess energy but also acts as a layer of insulation. Meanwhile, brown and beige fat contain specialised cells that burn energy to produce heat. This helps the body maintain its temperature. What happens when we have too little? The health consequences of having too much fat are well known. They include an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, certain cancers and osteoarthritis. However, having too little is not good either. When body fat drops too low due to severe calorie restriction, it can have profound effects on our health and physiology, explains Jessica Maung, a graduate student researcher of metabolic diseases at the University of Michigan. “Having too little adipose tissue leads to disrupted organ and bodily function,” she says. When the body has too little fat, it responds by trying to save energy, essentially putting itself into starvation mode. Systems start to shut down, including our immune function. With no reserves left, the body starts to break down muscle instead. Bones are no longer built and repaired. This results in frailty and increased risk of fractures, says Fredrik Karpe, professor of metabolic medicine at the University of Oxford. “That’s not a healthy situation,” says Karpe, especially because it leaves the body with no reserves to cope with a serious infection or other medical emergency. Too little body fat can affect our hormones and reproductive health too. In men who become extremely lean because they are chronically under-fuelling themselves, testosterone can fall, as can energy levels and physical performance. Some female athletes with very little body fat experience irregular periods or find that they stop altogether. Several studies have found that carrying extra weight in middle and older age is associated with better survival odds during a critical illness. For instance, while people living with obesity are more likely to suffer from cardiovascular disease, they are less likely to die from it than leaner individuals also suffering from the condition – a phenomenon known as the obesity paradox. A cushion of fat reserves appears to help the body withstand serious cardiac events, strokes and other acute illnesses, according to Oral. In extreme cases, having too little fat can lead to dire health consequences or be fatal. For example, the mental health condition anorexia nervosa can lead to long-term organ damage or death. How much do we really need? It’s surprisingly tricky to measure how much body fat you have yourself – but more on that later. There is also no universal percentage to aim for. Individual needs vary. Nevertheless, as a broad guide, healthy adult men tend to have around 10–20% body fat. Healthy adult women tend to have around 20–29%. Those living with obesity tend to have body fat above 30%. In terms of how much is optimal, “it’s very difficult to say exactly a range,” says Ryden. “This might differ between people, sex and ethnicities.” Among athletes, the typical amount of body fat tends to be lower. How to measure our fat There are a few ways to measure the amount of fat in your body. The most detailed assessments come from DEXA full-body scans, which can differentiate between body fat, lean muscle mass, and bone mass. However, these require specialist equipment and can be expensive. One popular home test is the skinfold test. This involves measuring the thickness of the fat layer just below the skin by pinching it using a specially designed pair of callipers. However, this instrument can only measure the thickness of fat folds at specific body parts. Visceral fat can’t be measured this way directly. But skinfold tests are not particularly accurate and may give misleadingly low figures.

items.title: Infantino promises more FIFA funding for African football
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA President Gianni Infantino has promised increased resources and continued support for African football, saying the governing body will look for additional funding to help the continent’s game reach the top of world football. According to Reuters, Infantino made the pledge while addressing presidents of Africa’s 54 football associations at a football strategy conference in Cape Verde on Thursday. Infantino highlighted FIFA’s financial contribution to African football since he became president in 2016, saying the FIFA Forward programme had invested $1 billion in the continent over the past decade. “With the FIFA Forward programme we have invested one billion dollars in 10 years in Africa, with 124 different projects and many other actions,” Infantino said. He said FIFA remained committed to creating more opportunities for African football and urged the Confederation of African Football (CAF) to communicate its needs so the governing body could provide further support. “Our commitment is to make sure that your football is going to continue to improve and grow, give you more opportunities,” he said. “Ten countries at the (last) World Cup has been a success for the entire continent. “We need to continue together on this path, because it is up to you as CAF to tell us what you want. How we can make you stronger and better.” Infantino also pledged to seek additional resources and increased funding for the continent. “We will continue to look for the resources and the increases (in funding) that are necessary to boost the African game to the top of world football,” he said. The FIFA president also called for open dialogue when concerns arise, saying the governing body was willing to address disagreements and improve its approach. “When you go through a journey, sometimes concerns are raised. When they are raised, we have to address them,” Infantino said. “As far as we are concerned at FIFA, we address them always with the spirit of dialogue and with open arms, an open heart and an open mind. We can always be better and do better.” The conference comes amid scrutiny of Infantino’s leadership following the July collapse of his proposal to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup. The plan faced opposition from mainly European and North American football nations, with some subsequently withdrawing their support for Infantino ahead of next year’s FIFA presidential election. The post Infantino promises more FIFA funding for African football appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le général-major Ali Sidane, nouveau commandant de la Gendarmerie nationale
items.description: Le général-major Ali Sidane est le nouveau commandant de la Gendarmerie nationale. Il a été installé dans ses nouvelles fonctions ce jeudi 8 octobre par le général d’armée Saïd Chanegriha, chef d’état-major de l’ANP, a indiqué le ministère de la Défense nationale dans un communiqué. Ali Sidane occupait jusqu’à lundi dernier le poste de chef de la 1ère région militaire, qu’il a cédé au général-major Noureddine Haddad. À la Gendarmerie, il remplace le général Sid Ali Berroumana qui était en poste depuis avril 2025. « Au nom de Monsieur le Président de la République, Chef suprême des Forces armées, ministre de la Défense nationale et conformément au décret présidentiel du 1er octobre 2026, j'installe officiellement le Général-major Ali Sidane, dans les fonctions de Commandant de la Gendarmerie nationale, en remplacement du Général-major Sid Ali Berroumana », a déclaré Saïd Chanegriha, dont les propos ont été rapportés dans le communiqué du MDN. Le chef d’état-major de l’ANP a ensuite tenu une rencontre avec les cadres et les personnels du Commandement de la Gendarmerie nationale, où il a prononcé une allocution d'orientation, diffusée par visioconférence à toutes les unités de la Gendarmerie nationale. Ce que Saïd Chanegriha a demandé aux gendarmes Saïd Chanegriha a souligné « l'importance vitale des missions assignées à la Gendarmerie nationale exige de chacun de veiller au renforcement constant des relations avec les citoyens, dont la confiance demeure l'une des principales sources de réussite dans l'accomplissement des missions ». « L'importance vitale des missions assignées à la Gendarmerie nationale exige de vous tous davantage d'attention dans leur accomplissement de la manière la plus parfaite. Cela nécessite de veiller, de façon consciente, au renforcement constant des liens avec les citoyens, dont la préservation de leur confiance demeure l'une des principales sources de réussite dans vos missions. À cet effet, il vous incombe d'accorder un intérêt particulier à cet aspect et lui donner l'importance et la priorité qu'il mérite », a-t-il demandé. Le chef d’état-major de l’ANP, qui occupe aussi le poste de ministre délégué auprès du ministre de la Défense nationale, a salué « le rôle important des unités de la Gendarmerie nationale, qui contribuent non seulement à la protection des frontières, à la lutte contre le terrorisme, la subversion, le narcotrafic et les crimes connexes, mais aussi à la protection des zones stratégiques et des points sensibles ». Il a ajouté que « la responsabilité de commander les hommes avec compétence professionnelle, intégrité et loyauté est une mission noble et importante, car elle exige pondération et clairvoyance dans la conduite des subordonnés ». L’article Le général-major Ali Sidane, nouveau commandant de la Gendarmerie nationale est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Bahrain working to 'speed up' approval of Pak-GCC free trade pact, foreign minister says
items.description: Bahrain on Thursday said it was working to “speed up” the approval of a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). The remarks came after the two countries held the third session of their Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad. Bahrain’s FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani — who arrived in Pakistan last night on a two-day visit — co-chaired the JMC session along with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. Addressing a joint press briefing with Dar, the Bahraini minister noted that the JMC meeting covered “more than 15 fields”. He said both sides agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment, as well as to convene the joint working group on energy next month on oil, gas and minerals. They also agreed to take forward cooperation in food security, information technology, law enforcement, media, labour mobility, health, education, culture and sports. “We also committed to finalising the GCC-Pakistan free trade agreement,” he said, referring to the potential deal that was said to be near finalisation in late 2025. The minister said that Bahrain, having the GCC presidency, was working to “speed up the signing or the approval of the GCC-Pakistan FTA”. Responding to a query, the visiting dignitary described the bilateral relationship between Pakistan and Bahrain as “very healthy and strong”. He added that it was “radiant and well-looked after” by Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa. “It is really valued by the people of Bahrain,” he added. Highlighting recent bilateral exchanges between their countries, FM Al Zayani said: “We have a very truthful relationship; we are so frank with each other. We understand the constraints on each other and work accordingly.” Emphasising the consistency in their ties, with no “ups and downs”, he said, “We are consistent and growing. We feel safe in this relationship.” Al Zayani expressed Manama’s appreciation for Islamabad’s “principled positions on the ongoing crisis”, including its support in March for a United Nations Security Council resolution condemning Iranian attacks on GCC countries. The minister also praised Pakistan’s “efforts alongside other partners to facilitate US-Iran dialogue and de-escalation, including by hosting the Islamabad Talks ” in April. The Bahrain FM went on to strongly condemn the recent deadly “terrorist attacks” on Saudi Arabia’s Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport. He also condemned the “Houthi terrorist militia’s attacks on civilians and civilian facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its assault” on the holy cities of Makkah and Madina . Noting that targeting of civilian facilities was a “flagrant violation” of international law, Al Zayani affirmed Bahrain’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia “whose security is an integral part of our own and of the GCC”. The Bahrain FM said he and Dar also discussed the crises in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, where “commercial vessels continue to come under attack”. They underscored the importance of freedom and safety of navigation and respect for international law, he added. Al Zayani vowed Bahrain and Pakistan will continue “close coordination” at the UNSC and between their Missions in New York. Furthermore, the visiting FM noted that the two countries will mark 55 years of diplomatic relations on Oct 14. Al Zayani remarked that the “bonds of brotherhood, trust and solidarity […] gained fresh momentum with the official visits to Bahrain” of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in November 2025 and of President Asif Ali Zardari in January this year. The minister noted that more than 140,000 Pakistanis in Bahrain contributed to its progress and “form a living bridge between our peoples”. The Bahrain FM said he would also meet with PM Shehbaz, President Zardari and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir during his visit. Gulf situation, Palestine, IWT discussed In his remarks, Dar thanked Al Zayani and his delegation for “their constructive engagement and their very valuable contribution to the success of today’s JMC session”. Noting that the discussions were held in a cordial and constructive atmosphere, he said both sides “reaffirmed our shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation across a broad spectrum of sectors”. “A key outcome of the session was the strengthening of our institutional framework through the operationalisation of several joint working groups,” Dar said, adding that these mechanisms will help ensure effective implementation of the decisions taken by the JMC. “Both sides also agreed to enhance cooperation in trade and investment promotion, industrial collaboration, agriculture and food security, skills development, higher education, information technology, logistics and maritime affairs, among many other areas.” They “particularly welcomed closer engagement between the business communities of the two countries”, the deputy premier added. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training and human resource development, with a view to creating new opportunities for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers. Dar noted that he and Al Zayani also exchanged views on the “evolving situation in the Gulf and emphasised the importance of restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy”. “We discussed the need to ensure the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab, given their importance to regional and global food and energy security.” The ministers also discussed the “grave situation in Palestine” and expressed concern over the “continued expansion of illegal settlements and attempts to alter the status of Al-Quds Al-Sharif”. Dar also raised the issue of India’s unilateral decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, terming it a “material breach of international law”. “Such actions jeopardise the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” the deputy premier stressed. “Pakistan-Bahrain friendship remains strong and forward-looking, and we are brotherly nations, with long fraternal ties, cooperating on international foras and meeting very frequently wherever we get an opportunity like brothers,” the DPM affirmed. He expressed Pakistan’s commitment to “building an even more prosperous future together, God-willing, and taking the trade and economic ties to a new height”. Dar said Islamabad looked forward to the convening of the JMC’s fourth session in Bahrain in 2027, as both sides will try to hold the meetings every year. President Zardari meets Bahrain FM Separately, President Zardari met with the Bahrain foreign minister, who called on him at the President House. According to a press release by the president’s secretariat, the two leaders first held a restricted meeting, which was followed by a delegation-level meeting. Zardari, in conversation with Al Zayani, said that Pakistan was “keen to translate strong bilateral political relations into deeper trade and investment ties”, according to the statement. Noting that the country attached “great importance” to its relations with Bahrain, he expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, highlighting opportunities for this cooperation in “food security, IT and digital services, construction, mining, port handling, research and development, tourism and healthcare”. He also encouraged greater business-to-business engagement between the two countries. “The president appreciated Bahrain’s warm welcome of the Islamabad MoU and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and its recognition of Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace, security and stability,” the press release said. It added that President Zardari also appreciated Bahrain’s support and opportunities for over 134,000 Pakistanis residing in the kingdom, and welcomed continued cooperation on matters regarding the Pakistani diaspora. “The president said Pakistan and Bahrain share a long-standing and trusted defence partnership, reflected in joint exercises, high-level exchanges and institutional cooperation,” it said, adding that he expressed Pakistan’s readiness to further strengthen cooperation in manpower, logistics, training and defence hardware. On the topic of the regional situation, he expressed Pakistan’s commitment to constructive engagement with all parties to “build trust, bridge gaps and promote lasting peace, security and stability in the region”. During the meeting, Al Zayani conveyed the greetings of King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the crown prince and prime minister of Bahrain, to the president, the statement added. He termed the JMC meetings “highly productive” and noted that the president’s visit to Bahrain had left “a significant and positive impact on bilateral relations”. He commended Pakistan’s courageous efforts to mediate amid the current regional situation and bring warring parties to the table, saying that Pakistan’s actions had “helped save many lives”. He appreciated Pakistan’s peace efforts and congratulated it on its successful tenure as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council. Meeting with PM Shehbaz The foreign minister also called on PM Shehbaz, who warmly welcomed him and conveyed his best wishes to the leadership and people of Bahrain, according to a press release by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). He reaffirmed Pakistan’s “deep appreciation for the longstanding and brotherly relations between Pakistan and Bahrain, founded on shared values, mutual trust, and close people-to-people ties”, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz expressed his satisfaction over the positive trajectory of bilateral relations. He emphasised Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Bahrain in diverse fields, “including trade, investment, energy, and human resource development”. FM Al-Zayani, meanwhile, conveyed the greetings and well-wishes of the leadership of Bahrain to the premier, and reaffirmed Bahrain’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across mutually beneficial areas. “The two sides exchanged views on regional and international developments and emphasised the importance of continued consultations and coordination on issues of mutual interest,” the statement said. Al-Zayani “appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and mediation efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”, the PMO added. The prime minister expressed confidence that the JMC session would provide “further impetus” to bilateral cooperation and help deepen the relationship between the two countries. “The meeting was held in a warm and cordial atmosphere, reflecting the close and longstanding fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain,” the statement added. JMC meeting During the JMC meeting, Islamabad and Manama “agreed to deepen collaboration in trade and investment, energy, agriculture and food security, information technology, health, education and labour”, FO said. They also discussed measures to strengthen connectivity and promote people-to-people exchanges. Dar “underscored the importance of translating the longstanding and fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain into tangible benefits for their people”. He further stressed effective implementation of the agreed outcomes through joint working groups, institutional partnerships and regular follow-up, FO added. The JMC was attended by high-level delegations from both sides. The Pakistani team included the secretaries of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and the Economic Affairs Division, along with the acting foreign secretary. The Bahraini side included senior officials and representatives of the Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry. In his address to the JMC meeting, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to increase bilateral trade with Bahrain to the $1 billion target set earlier . Noting the target of doubling trade in three years, of which one has already elapsed, Dar quipped, “But God forbid, if we miss [the target by] a few months, we have a great excuse that this period has been very turbulent.” Dar also referred to the potential Pakistan-GCC FTA, noting that the GCC secretary general told him the deal was “almost ripe”, with one country yet to give a green light to it. “I’m sure the signing of the free trade agreement between the GCC and Pakistan will surely help us in achieving our goals,” the deputy premier said, adding that it would lead to an increase in imports and exports. He requested the Bahraini side to work towards recognising degrees and professional qualifications, while facilitating greater mobility of skilled labour between the two countries. The two ministers also signed a protocol recording the minutes of the JMC session at the foreign ministry, according to the FO. “The minutes record understandings on cooperation in trade and investment, agriculture and food security, oil, gas and minerals, maritime affairs, information technology and telecommunications, health, education and labour, among other areas,” the FO said in a separate statement. It added that both sides agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment at the government level, as an institutional mechanism for “regular consultations, coordination and cooperation on bilateral trade and investment”. Bilateral meeting Prior to the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, the two foreign ministers also held a separate meeting after Al Zayani’s arrival at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In a post on X about the “cordial” meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said the two ministers “reviewed Pakistan–Bahrain relations and expressed satisfaction at the positive momentum in high-level engagement between the two countries”. “They discussed ways to further expand bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual interest, particularly in trade, economic and investment relations, as well as through engagement at multilateral fora.” The two sides also exchanged views on “regional and international developments of mutual interest and underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain the most viable means of addressing challenges and resolving disputes”, the FO added. According to an earlier FO statement, the two sides were to “review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen cooperation across diverse areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, economic cooperation, defence and security, labour and manpower, and cultural exchanges”. “Pakistan and Bahrain enjoy close, brotherly relations founded on shared faith, common values, mutual respect, and longstanding people-to-people links,” FO noted. Dar and Al Zayani last met in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the JMC session. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, with Al Zayani appreciating Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability. Pak-Bahrain exchanges Islamabad and Manama had agreed to establish the JMC in 2014, when King Sheikh Hamad bin Isa bin Salman Al-Khalifa paid a three-day visit to Pakistan. Following the last JMC session in July 2021, which was held in Manama, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries. Earlier this month, Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting to review preparations for the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC and directed the ministries concerned to pursue concrete outcomes from the Bahrain FM’s visit. The Pakistani leadership has also undertaken official visits to the Gulf kingdom in recent years. PM Shehbaz, accompanied by Dar, made a two-day trip to Bahrain in November 2025, during which he met with the king and crown prince there. Then, in January this year, President Zardari made a four-day trip to the kingdom, where he highlighted economic opportunities that Pakistan offers.

items.title: Amnesty urges Madonna University to reverse students’ sanctions
items.description: PORT HARCOURT — Amnesty International Nigeria has urged the authorities of Madonna University, Elele Campus, Rivers State, to rescind the expulsion of a final-year nursing student and the suspension of 14 other 500-level students over a viral TikTok video. The rights organisation made the call in a post on its X platform on Thursday, describing the expulsion and suspensions as disproportionate. Amnesty International urged the university to prioritise dialogue and mediation in resolving the matter, warning that heavy-handed academic or disciplinary sanctions could jeopardise the students’ academic progress. According to the organisation, the affected students have rights to freedom of expression, academic freedom and education. It said the expulsion and suspensions were harsh and could create a chilling effect on the exercise of those rights. “Amnesty International urges the authorities of Madonna University Elele Campus, Rivers State, to rescind the expulsion of a final-year nursing student and the suspension of 14 other 500-level students over a viral TikTok video,” the organisation said. “The expulsion and suspension are disproportionate.” Amnesty International further called on the university to ensure that its policies and disciplinary procedures conform to international human rights standards. It urged the institution to uphold the rights of all students, particularly their rights to freedom of expression, education and academic freedom. items.title: Arsenal’s 16-year-old Dowman gets three Guinness World Records certificates
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Arsenal teenager Max Dowman has been presented with three official Guinness World Records certificates after setting new marks in English and European football before turning 17. Guinness World Records announced the recognition on its official X handle on Thursday, celebrating Dowman’s record-breaking rise with the Arsenal first team. “Three Guinness World Records titles before 17,” Guinness World Records posted. “@Arsenal’s Max Dowman has been presented with three official Guinness World Records certificates following his record-breaking rise through English and European football.” Dowman, who turns 17 in December, holds the record for the youngest player to appear in the UEFA Champions League, having featured for Arsenal against Slavia Prague at 15 years and 308 days. He also became the youngest Premier League goalscorer when he scored against Everton at 16 years and 73 days. Dowman completed his trio of records by becoming the youngest player to win the Premier League, collecting his winner’s medal at 16 years and 144 days after Arsenal secured the title. He was part of Arsenal’s breakthrough 2025-26 campaign, making 13 senior appearances as the club won their first Premier League title since 2004. Dowman’s record-breaking Premier League goal came in memorable fashion as he ran from his own half, beat two players and finished into an empty net after Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford had gone forward for a corner. The teenager has continued to make an impact this season, scoring twice in Arsenal’s 4-2 Carabao Cup victory over Ipswich in September. Dowman was also featured in the Guinness World Records Football Edition 2027, released on Thursday, as part of its “Class of ’27”. items.title: JESA accompagne le Sénégal dans la structuration de son réseau gazier national
items.description: JESA, acteur majeur dans la livraison de projets et fournisseur de solutions intégrées au Maroc et en Afrique, accompagne le Réseau Gazier du Sénégal S.A. (RGS), filiale de PETROSEN HOLDING, dans le développement et la préparation à l’exploitation du futur réseau national de transport de gaz naturel du Sénégal, une infrastructure stratégique de près de 400 km destinée à connecter les ressources gazières offshore du pays à ses centres de production électrique et à ses zones industrielles. Dans le cadre de cette mission d’Assistance à Maîtrise d’Ouvrage (AMO), JESA agit en qualité de mandataire et de chef de file d’un consortium réunissant OMCo, filiale de l’Office National des Hydrocarbures et des Mines (ONHYM), gestionnaire du Gazoduc Maghreb Europe (GME) et Antea Group France. Le consortium accompagne RGS durant les phases de développement et de gestion des travaux de construction, de mise en service et d’exploitation du réseau national. La cérémonie officielle de pose de la première canalisation du Segment Nord, organisée le 10 septembre 2026 à SaintLouis sous la présidence de Dr El Hadji Abdourahmane Diouf, ministre de l’Énergie et du Pétrole du Sénégal, marque une étape structurante dans la concrétisation de ce programme stratégique. Cette journée a notamment réuni Pape Momar Lo, Directeur Général de RGS, Omar Benjelloun, Directeur Général de JESA West Africa, Abderrahim Ben Elhirche, Directeur Exécutif Senior, Energie de JESA et Mohammed Benzaria, Directeur Général d’OMCo, représentant de Amina Benkhadra, Directrice Générale de l’ONHYM et Présidente d’OMCo. Un programme structurant pour la souveraineté énergétique sénégalaise Porté par RGS SA – société détenue par PETROSEN HOLDING (51 %), FONSIS (39 %) et Senelec (10 %) –, ce projet s’inscrit au cœur des stratégies nationales « Gas to Power » et « Gas to Industry » du Sénégal. Le futur réseau permettra de connecter les ressources gazières offshore du pays, entre autres, aux infrastructures de production électrique et aux futurs usages industriels, en assurant notamment l’acheminement du gaz naturel issu du champ Grand Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA), développé conjointement par le Sénégal et la Mauritanie. À travers ce programme structurant, le Sénégal entend valoriser ses ressources gazières au bénéfice de sa population, renforcer sa sécurité énergétique et soutenir durablement son développement économique et son industrialisation. « Ce programme illustre la manière dont des expertises africaines complémentaires peuvent se mobiliser au service d’une priorité nationale structurante. En accompagnant RGS, JESA réaffirme son engagement aux côtés du Sénégal et, plus largement, son ambition de contribuer au développement d’infrastructures énergétiques capables de soutenir durablement l’industrialisation, la compétitivité et l’intégration régionale en Afrique de l’Ouest » déclare Monsieur Omar Benjelloun, Directeur Général de JESA West Africa. Une assistance couvrant l’ensemble des enjeux techniques et opérationnels Mandataire et chef de file du consortium chargé de la mission d’Assistance à Maîtrise d’Ouvrage, JESA accompagne RGS dans le développement de son futur réseau national et prépare, dès les premières phases du projet, les conditions nécessaires à une exploitation sûre, fiable et performante. À ce titre, JESA mobilise ses expertises en ingénierie, en gestion de projets et en assurance de la performance de réalisation. Son intervention couvre notamment l’appui aux processus de contractualisation, la supervision technique, le suivi des délais et des risques, la coordination des interfaces ainsi que l’accompagnement à la préparation opérationnelle du réseau. « Notre responsabilité, en tant que mandataire et chef de file du consortium, est de sécuriser chaque étape du programme en combinant rigueur technique, pilotage des interfaces, maîtrise des risques et anticipation des futures conditions d’exploitation. L’enjeu est de préparer non seulement la réalisation du réseau, mais aussi sa performance durable, sa disponibilité et son intégrité sur l’ensemble de son cycle de vie » , souligne Abderrahim Ben Elhirche, Directeur Exécutif Senior, Energie de JESA. OMCo, une expertise au service des coopérations énergétiques africaines Pour OMCo, filiale de l’ONHYM, la mission menée auprès de RGS s’inscrit dans la continuité de son engagement en faveur du développement des infrastructures gazières et du partage d’expertise à l’échelle du continent. Une dynamique de coopération énergétique maroco-sénégalaise Cette collaboration entre acteurs marocains contribue à positionner le Maroc comme un partenaire technique de référence pour le développement des infrastructures gazières en Afrique de l’Ouest et à renforcer la crédibilité et la visibilité de son savoir-faire dans le secteur énergétique. Au-delà de sa portée technique, cette initiative consolide les partenariats institutionnels entre le Maroc et le Sénégal et traduit une ambition partagée : mobiliser les expertises africaines au service du développement des infrastructures énergétiques du continent, dans le cadre d’une coopération durable fondée sur la complémentarité des savoir-faire et le renforcement des capacités locales. Elle s’inscrit pleinement dans la vision du Roi Mohammed VI, visant à promouvoir l’intégration énergétique et le développement économique de la façade atlantique africaine. JESA, un partenaire clé de la transformation énergétique africaine Pour JESA, la mission menée auprès de RGS s’inscrit dans une ambition plus large : accompagner les grandes transitions énergétiques et industrielles du continent africain en mettant son expertise internationale, sa connaissance approfondie des réalités locales et ses capacités intégrées en ingénierie et en gestion de programmes complexes au service des priorités nationales de développement. Cette dynamique s’inscrit dans la continuité de plusieurs projets énergétiques majeurs auxquels JESA contribue dans la sous-région, notamment au Sénégal et au Bénin, ainsi que dans le développement de projets liés à l’hydrogène en Mauritanie. La mission RGS renforce ainsi la présence de JESA sur le marché de l’énergie en Afrique de l’Ouest et confirme son rôle de partenaire de confiance dans la réalisation d’infrastructures complexes à fort impact. The post JESA accompagne le Sénégal dans la structuration de son réseau gazier national appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: NAF crash: Families of victims will get support — Chief of the Air Staff
items.description: …orders high-level probe into crash that killed 25 By Dayo Johnson AKURE — The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, has ordered a high-level investigation into the Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, which claimed 25 lives. Aneke, who visited the crash site, also assured the families of the deceased that the Nigerian Armed Forces would provide them with the necessary support. The aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, was on a routine flight from Benin to Lagos when it crashed into a swampy area opposite the Naval Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda. All 25 people on board, including the crew, died in the crash. Recovery hampered by swampy terrain About 96 hours after the accident, the main body of the aircraft was yet to be excavated, while the remains of the victims had not been fully recovered. The flight recorder, popularly known as the black box, which could provide vital information on the circumstances surrounding the crash, had also not been recovered. This was despite the deployment of heavy-duty amphibious excavators, known as swamp buggies, to the crash site by the Ondo State Government. The equipment arrived with technical personnel and specialised detection equipment to help locate the submerged wreckage. The crash site, located about 500 metres east of the Naval Forward Operating Base, has proved difficult to access because of its swampy terrain. Initial recovery attempts using small boats and canoes were reportedly inadequate. Only fragments of the aircraft had been recovered as of the time of filing this report. Air Chief orders comprehensive probe Aneke said he had directed the Superintendent of Safety and Evaluation to assemble a high-level team comprising military and civilian safety experts to investigate the crash. “I have informed my Superintendent of Safety and Evaluation to come up with a high-level delegation comprising of both military and civilian safety experts, NTSB, Accident and Emergency Management Board, retired senior officers, experienced Air Force officers, to sit down and get to the bottom of what happened,” he said. The Air Chief urged members of the public to avoid speculation on the cause of the crash until the investigation was concluded. “This is not the time to start speculating, and I plead with you, general public. We’ve lost people who are fighting for the nation,” he said. “The best we can do for them is to be a little bit patient and let those who are the specialists get to the bottom of what has happened.” Aneke said aviation safety remained a priority for the Nigerian Air Force, adding that the service would leave no stone unturned in determining what led to the accident. “It’s a very big loss, and no amount of words we put can bring so-called understanding to those who have lost. I myself have grieved, so I understand how it feels,” he said. ‘Families will get necessary support’ The Chief of the Air Staff assured the families of the deceased that the Nigerian Air Force would provide the necessary assistance. “The Nigerian Air Force is putting everything possible to ensure that the families get the necessary support they need,” Aneke said. He commended the Ondo State Government and residents of Igbokoda for their response to the disaster. “I have inspected the crash site. I want to use this opportunity to thank first the good people of Ondo State and our governor. They have committed resources, time and energy,” he said. “The locals here, the residents here, were the first responders. I’ve been briefed by the commander of the Navy here. “Words cannot describe how we Nigerians come together when things go south.” ‘I knew everyone on board’ While sympathising with the families of the victims, Aneke said the tragedy was particularly painful to him because he personally knew those on board. “On behalf of the President, Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, and also officers and men of the Nigerian Armed Forces, I want to first express our deep sorrow and condolence to the families who have lost their loved ones in this tragic incident,” he said. “I basically knew everyone on that flight. I’ve flown on this aeroplane. My family has flown on this aeroplane. I know each of the crew personally. “Highly trained, professional, and intelligent officers. The best we can do is to honour the sacrifice of those on board this aeroplane.” Aneke assured the bereaved families that the military would continue to stand by them. “I want to assure the families of our loved ones that the Nigerian Armed Forces will stand guard in ensuring that you are safe,” he said. The post NAF crash: Families of victims will get support — Chief of the Air Staff appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Volontariat senior au Burkina Faso : Le GIP-PNVB échange avec les aînés sur les modalités de mobilisation
items.description: Le Groupement d’intérêt public-Programme national de volontariat au Burkina Faso (GIP-PNVB) a rencontré, ce 8 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, les volontaires seniors. Cette rencontre a été l’occasion d’échanger directement avec eux sur les modalités de mise en œuvre de la mobilisation. En vue de mieux comprendre les attentes des volontaires seniors et de présenter plus clairement la vision, les objectifs ainsi que les modalités de mise en œuvre du volontariat senior, le Groupement d’intérêt public-Programme national de volontariat au Burkina Faso (GIP-PNVB) a organisé une rencontre avec les concernés. Selon le directeur général du GIP-PNVB, Djourmité Nestor Noufé, il s’agit d’une rencontre de prise de contact qui intervient après le lancement de l’initiative, le vendredi 25 septembre 2026. « Nous souhaitons que cette initiative soit construite avec vous et qu’elle puisse s’appuyer sur vos propositions, vos expériences et vos suggestions afin de répondre au mieux aux réalités et aux besoins de notre pays » , a-t-il déclaré. Selon le Directeur général du GIP-PNVB, Djourmité Nestor Noufé, il s’agit d’une rencontre de prise de contact qui intervient après le lancement de l’initiative le vendredi 25 septembre 2026. Ces volontaires présentent des profils variés. Il s’agit de travailleurs à la retraite, mais également de travailleurs encore en activité et comptant plus de 20 ans de service. Les fonctionnaires de l’État n’en font toutefois pas partie. « Le dispositif ne permet pas qu’un fonctionnaire de l’État qui a un contrat en cours puisse être volontaire, parce que nous allons signer un contrat avec ceux qui seront recrutés comme volontaires » , a-t-il expliqué. De l’avis du président du Conseil d’administration du GIP-PNVB, Mahamoudou Zan, le volontariat est un acte citoyen et patriotique qui ne concerne aucune catégorie sociale, professionnelle ou d’âge particulière. C’est pourquoi, dans ce contexte de Révolution progressiste populaire et de reconquête de la souveraineté, il est nécessaire de bénéficier de l’appui des aînés et des personnes expérimentées dans le domaine du volontariat. « Dans vos domaines de compétences respectifs, à travers vos métiers, votre parcours et vos savoirs accumulés, vous avez pour mission d'être les mentors de notre jeunesse. »,Mahamoudou Zan. Leur mobilisation, à travers cette initiative, constitue une manière pour le Groupement d’intérêt public-Programme national de volontariat au Burkina Faso de valoriser l’expérience et les compétences des anciens, en favorisant une transmission efficace des savoirs. « Dans vos domaines de compétences respectifs, à travers vos métiers, votre parcours et vos savoirs accumulés, vous avez pour mission d'être les mentors de notre jeunesse. Encadrer, conseiller, accompagner ces jeunes hommes et femmes qui brûlent d'envie de se battre pour le pays, c'est leur donner les armes de la rigueur, de la méthode et de la conscience professionnelle » , a-t-il déclaré. À travers cette mobilisation, le Groupement d’intérêt public-Programme national de volontariat au Burkina Faso veut mettre en œuvre une phase pilote reposant sur deux axes. Le premier axe concerne la santé, avec la sélection de 15 volontaires qui seront mobilisés et mis à la disposition de l’hôpital Saint-Camille dans le cadre d’Octobre rose. Le second concerne sept profils dans les domaines des finances, de la banque et de la gestion de projets, afin d’accompagner 35 volontaires et post-volontaires porteurs de projets dans différents domaines d’activité. Parmi ces volontaires séniors, on trouve des retraités et des agents en activités avec plusieurs profils. Parmi ces volontaires seniors figurent des agents de santé, des agents de recouvrement, des gestionnaires, des techniciens, des membres des Forces de défense et de sécurité, des sociologues, des secrétaires, des ingénieurs, des entrepreneurs, d’anciens VDP nationaux, des administrateurs civils ainsi que des enseignants. Au 7 octobre 2026, la plateforme avait enregistré 424 volontaires seniors depuis le lancement de l’initiative, le 25 septembre 2026. items.title: 10 phones with the fastest charging speeds, from 120W to 240W
items.description: By Mmesoma Goodness When we talk about charging speeds, we’re basically looking at how long it takes for a phone to go from nearly empty, around 1% to fully charged. Wired charging is usually much faster, while wireless takes a bit longer. We also check shorter intervals, like 15 or 30 minutes, since many of us just top up our phones between errands or meetings. Seeing how much charge you get in a short burst gives a clearer picture of real-world performance. It also shows which phones are the most convenient to use. Charging wattage and actual charging time aren’t exactly the same, because battery size and charging curves matter too. The following phones shows how the charging speed can be: Realme GT3 The Realme GT3 is famous for its 240W wired charging, one of the fastest charging technologies ever put into a smartphone. Its 4,600mAh battery can be charged from 0–100% in roughly 9–10 minutes under ideal conditions. It also features a 6.74-inch AMOLED display and a high-performance Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 processor. Realme GT5 240W The Realme GT5 240W is another 240W charging powerhouse. Its 4,600mAh battery can be fully charged in around 10 minutes. It combines this extreme charging speed with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 chipset, a high-refresh-rate AMOLED display and a gaming-focused design. Redmi Note 12 Explorer The Redmi Note 12 Explorer supports 210W fast charging, allowing its 4,300mAh battery to reach full charge in only about 9 minutes in laboratory conditions. It was one of the earliest mainstream phones to demonstrate extremely high charging speeds. iQOO 10 Pro The iQOO 10 Pro features 200W wired charging, capable of charging its 4,700mAh battery in approximately 10 minutes. It is designed as a high-performance phone, featuring a Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 processor and a 2K AMOLED display. OnePlus 10T The OnePlus 10T supports up to 150W SUPERVOOC charging in markets where the full charging standard is available. Its 4,800mAh battery can be charged extremely quickly. It also uses the Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 chipset, making it a strong performance-oriented smartphone. OnePlus 10R The OnePlus 10R is available in a 150W SUPERVOOC version. Its 4,500mAh battery can be charged from empty to full in around 17 minutes. It also features a MediaTek Dimensity 8100-MAX processor and a 120Hz AMOLED display. Realme GT Neo 3 150W The GT Neo 3 150W introduced Realme’s 150W UltraDart charging technology. Its 4,500mAh battery can reach 100% in roughly 17 minutes. It is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 8100 and was particularly popular among users looking for fast performance at a relatively affordable price. RedMagic 7 Pro The RedMagic 7 Pro is a gaming smartphone with 135W charging in some markets. It combines fast charging with gaming-focused hardware, including an active cooling fan, high-refresh-rate display and Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 processor. Motorola Edge 40 Pro The Motorola Edge 40 Pro supports 125W TurboPower charging. Its 4,600mAh battery can be rapidly replenished, making it convenient for users who need quick top-ups. It also features a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor, a 165Hz display and a premium design. Xiaomi 12 Pro The Xiaomi 12 Pro supports 120W HyperCharge, allowing its 4,600mAh battery to charge very rapidly. It also offers a 2K AMOLED 120Hz display, Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 processor and a triple 50MP rear-camera system.
