items.title: Mali : l’armée reprend le contrôle de la ville stratégique de Kidal avec le soutien du Corps africain du ministère russe de la Défense
items.description: Les Forces armees maliennes (FAMa), avec le soutien du Corps africain du ministere russe de la Defense, ont repris le controle de Kidal, dans le nord-est du pays, a l'issue d'une operation militaire menee du 1er au 7 octobre 2026. Bastion historique de la rebellion touareg, cette ville strategique etait passee en avril sous le controle du Front de liberation de l'Azawad (FLA) et de ses allies du Groupe de soutien a l'islam et aux musulmans (JNIM ou GSIM), une organisation djihadiste affiliee a Al-Qaïda. La reprise de Kidal constitue une avancee pour Bamako dans ses efforts pour restaurer l'autorite de l'etat dans le nord du pays. L'operation a reuni les forces maliennes et les unites russes du Corps africain, avec l'appui du Groupe d'autodefense touareg Imghad et allies (GATIA) et du Mouvement pour le salut de l'Azawad (MSA), deux mouvements progouvernementaux. Elle illustre leur cooperation militaire dans la lutte contre les groupes armes presents dans la region. Une offensive appuyee par les moyens militaires russes Selon un communique du Corps africain, les forces alliees ont parcouru plus de 450 kilometres depuis Gao, franchissant des terrains accidentes et des zones minees, tout en recuperant plusieurs localites sur leur passage. Cette progression s'est accompagnee d'operations aeriennes menees de concert par les forces maliennes et russes. D'apres le Corps africain, les frappes ont cause d'importants dommages aux positions adverses autour de Kidal, ainsi qu'a leurs installations dans les secteurs d'Abeïbara, Tin-Essako, Talhandak, Tin Zaouatine et Tessalit. La reconnaissance aerienne a aussi joue un role dans la marche des troupes. a une trentaine de kilometres a l'ouest de Kidal, un drone a repere un groupe arme preparant une embuscade contre une colonne alliee. Selon le Corps africain, les combattants et leurs vehicules camoufles ont ete detruits. Face a l'offensive conjointe, les combattants separatistes ont quitte Kidal. Le FLA a confirme son retrait, le presentant comme un « repli strategique », motive, selon lui, par la volonte de preserver ses effectifs et les civils des frappes aeriennes. Le 6 octobre, les forces maliennes sont entrees dans la ville sans rencontrer de resistance directe. Des responsables militaires ont explique que les frappes menees en amont avaient affaibli le dispositif adverse et facilite l'arrivee des troupes. Securisation et retablissement de l'autorite de Bamako Le 7 octobre, les militaires maliens et russes poursuivaient les operations de securisation. Le Corps africain fait etat de lourdes pertes parmi leurs adversaires. Des actions de deminage et d'assistance humanitaire ont par ailleurs ete engagees dans une ville largement depeuplee. Au-dela de l'operation militaire, cette reprise revet une importance politique et symbolique. Dans son communique, le Corps africain souligne que la ville represente l'un des principaux emblemes de l'etat malien dans le nord du pays. Cette reconquete permet a Bamako de reprendre pied dans une cite strategique, apres plusieurs mois d'occupation par les groupes armes. Elle temoigne aussi de l'engagement operationnel du Corps africain aux cotes des forces maliennes dans cette offensive.

items.title: «La Paki» : après les «Mamadou» et les «rabzouz», Macron se voit à nouveau prêter des propos racistes
items.description: Alors qu'une grande partie de la presse francaise a les yeux rives sur des propos a connotation antisemite que Jordan Bardella aurait tenus lors de sa puberte, selon Mediapart, L'Infiltre est venu jeter un pave dans la mare. D'apres l'hebdomadaire d'investigation, recemment lance par le media Frontieres (ex-Livre noir), la campagne de Gabriel Attal serait devenue un « sujet de plaisanterie recurrent » a l'elysee, ou l'on suivrait la tournee des « mille bistrots » avec « une gourmandise peu fraternelle ». Un exercice auquel « participe lui-meme » le chef de l'etat francais, peut-on lire, notamment aux depens de Prisca Thevenot, deputee Ensemble des Hauts-de-Seine, ex-porte-parole du gouvernement Attal et soutien de ce dernier dans la campagne pour l'election presidentielle de 2027. « Un temoin de la scene rapporte a L'Infiltre que Macron s'est moque de la deputee alors qu'elle intervenait en duplex a la television pour defendre la campagne d'Attal, en l'appelant "la Paki" », a ainsi relate l'hebdomadaire. « Je n'imagine pas que de tels mots puissent avoir ete tenus reellement. Il faut qu'il y ait un dementi rapide », a reagi sur X le 7 octobre la deputee Ensemble du Nord Violette Spillebout et porte-parole de Gabriel Attal. Meme tonalite du cote de son homologue de la Sarthe Julie Delpech. « J'espere qu'ils sont faux et qu'un dementi sera rapidement apporte », a declare cette autre deputee du parti presidentiel, semblant elle aussi oublier que ce n'est pas la premiere fois que des propos de ce genre sont pretes au locataire du 55 rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honore. Je découvre cet article qui rapporte des propos racistes prêtés au Président de la République, à l’encontre de notre collègue @priscathevenot. Je n’imagine pas que de tels mots puissent avoir été tenus réellement. Il faut qu’il y ait un démenti rapide. Ne jamais laisser passer le racisme, l’antisemitisme, la discrimination. — Violette Spillebout (@VSpillebout) October 7, 2026 Fin 2024, Le Monde rapportait qu'Emmanuel Macron aurait – notamment – declare a son ministre de la Sante de l'epoque Aurelien Rousseau que les urgences en France sont « rempli[es] de Mamadou ». Toujours selon le quotidien, le president francais qualifierait aussi les Maghrebins de « rabzouz ». Des revelations qui avaient provoque un tolle a gauche de l'echiquier politique francais. « Les propos racistes du president Macron le rendent indigne d'exercer sa fonction. Notre appel a la destitution est sur la table, celles et ceux qui sont attaches aux principes de la Republique doivent s'en saisir », avait fustige la vice-presidente La France insoumise (LFI) de l'Assemblee nationale Clemence Guette. Des propos rapportes que l'elysee s'etait contente de « fermement » dementir, selon les declarations de « l'entourage » d'Emmanuel Macron… eux-memes rapportes par Le Monde , qui avait « mainten[u] ses informations ». Propos bien plus difficiles a dementir en revanche : ceux tenus par le president francais quelques semaines apres son election en 2017, lorsqu'il lâchait tout sourire et face camera que le « kwassa-kwassa » – frele esquif que l'on retrouve dans l'archipel des Comores – « peche peu, il amene du Comorien » a Mayotte. Dans ses revelations de decembre 2024, Le Monde s'etait aussi attarde sur la maniere dont Emmanuel Macron qualifiait de « cocottes » la secretaire nationale des ecologistes Marine Tondelier et Lucie Castets, alors designee par le Nouveau Front populaire (NFP) pour devenir Premiere ministre, ou encore sur la facon dont il avait rebaptise Matignon, sous Gabriel Attal, « cage aux folles ».

items.title: Three suspected illegal miners arrested in Tano-Boin Forest Reserve
items.description: Three men suspected of illegally mining in the Tano-Boin Forest Reserve have been arrested and remanded after allegedly being caught operating along the bank of the Tano River. The suspects were arrested on Friday, October 2, 2026, by members of the Jema Anti-Galamsey Advocacy (JAGA) Watch Committee during an operation in the protected forest reserve. According to JAGA, the suspects were found with a water-pumping machine and a changfang mining raft. One of the suspects allegedly attempted to escape by swimming across the Tano River after the committee members intercepted them. Members of the Watch Committee pursued him into the river and apprehended him. Following the arrests, the three suspects were handed over to the Police at the Jema Police Station and later transferred to the District Police Command at Enchi. However, because the Enchi Magistrate and Circuit Courts currently do not have substantive judicial officers, the suspects were taken to the Assankragwa Magistrate Court, where they were remanded for one week. JAGA commended the Enchi District Police Command, particularly District Commander Chief Superintendent Mensah, for ensuring that the suspects were brought before a court. The organisation said the District and Regional offices of the Forestry Commission at Enchi and Wiawso were immediately informed of the arrests. The Forestry Commission subsequently arranged transportation for the suspects from Jema to Enchi and covered other operational expenses incurred during the operation. JAGA said Forestry Commission officials have assured the organisation that they will follow up on the case to ensure that the suspects are dealt with in accordance with the law. JAGA said the latest case highlights the need for sustained enforcement against illegal mining in protected forest reserves and greater collaboration between community watchdogs and state institutions. The organisation said it expects the relevant law-enforcement and judicial authorities to give the case the necessary attention because of the environmental implications of illegal mining in forest reserves. It also commended the Attorney General and the Chief Justice for initiatives to establish special courts to expedite the prosecution of galamsey-related cases in selected regional capitals, including Sekondi. “When civilians risk their lives to arrest illegal miners to protect their water bodies and forests from destruction, state institutions must support them by enforcing the law,” JAGA said. The organisation maintained that the protection of Ghana’s forests and water bodies requires collaboration among security agencies, the Judiciary, politicians, traditional leaders and local communities. JAGA also appealed to the media and international environmental organisations to follow the case to help ensure that proceedings are handled transparently and in accordance with the law. The organisation contrasted the latest arrests with an earlier case involving two Nigerien nationals who were arrested last year for allegedly mining in the Jema-Assemkrom Forest Reserve. According to JAGA, those suspects were later granted police bail, with the organisation saying it has since seen little progress in the case. JAGA said the latest development reinforces the importance of ensuring that arrests linked to illegal mining proceed through the appropriate legal and judicial channels.

items.title: Ondo aircraft crash: Deceased officers are highly trained professionals — Chief of Air Staff
items.description: AKURE — The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has described the Nigerian Air Force personnel killed in Monday’s aircraft crash in Ondo State as highly trained professionals, saying the circumstances surrounding the incident would be thoroughly investigated. Aneke spoke on Thursday when he visited the scene of the crash at Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area of the state. The Air Force chief said it was too early to speculate on the cause of the crash, stressing that experts and investigators would work to establish exactly what happened. He said: “They are highly trained professional officers. I know them personally. All the officers, I know everyone.” “Whatever happened here will be properly investigated. We must sit down to get what happened. This is not the time to speculate what happened. We must get to the root of this.” Aneke described the incident as a major loss to the Nigerian Air Force and the families of the deceased personnel. “It’s a very big loss. I am bereaved and no amount of words can be enough to calm the relatives of the victims,” he said. The Chief of the Air Staff also assured the families of the deceased that the Nigerian Air Force would not abandon them, adding that efforts would be made to recover the wreckage and determine the cause of the accident. He said, “I assure Nigerians that we will make sure to get the wreckages of the aircraft and get to the root of it. We will make sure that nothing of this will happen again. “I assure the families that they will not be left alone. Air Force will be responsible to the families and make sure that children and families are taken care of.” Aneke also commended the dedication and professionalism of the personnel involved in the operation, as well as the support provided by sister security agencies, government authorities and local communities. He specifically appreciated the police and other security agencies for their assistance in the response to the crash. The Air Force chief had earlier commended the personnel involved in the operation for their dedication and professionalism, while expressing appreciation to all those who contributed to the response and recovery efforts. The post Ondo aircraft crash: Deceased officers are highly trained professionals — Chief of Air Staff appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AratheJay brings Nimo Live Experience to Cape Coast on October 11
items.description: Ghanaian Highlife and Afro-fusion artiste AratheJay will perform live at XCape Beach Resort in Cape Coast on Sunday, 11 October. The singer, born Samuel Ofei Ankrah Badu, says the concert will be a special moment for the Central Region, as it marks his first-ever live performance in the historic city. “This will be a special moment for the people of Cape Coast, because for the first ever time, I’m going to have a show there. It’s going to be a live band performance,” AratheJay said. The Cape Coast show forms part of a nationwide city tour leading up to his major headline concert in Accra this December. According to the artiste, the tour is designed to give fans an intimate experience of his evolving sound. “We are leading the audience to an experience which is going to happen in December in Accra. But before that, we are going to touch a couple of cities, so we just came from Kumasi, we do Cape Coast and hopeful another city before closing the year with Nimo Live Experience in Accra,” he explained. The award-winning crooner promised fans in Cape Coast an unforgettable night with his live band, featuring some of his biggest records. Fans should expect AratheJay to unleash countless hit songs to create an irresistible atmosphere. He described the upcoming concert as a deeper connection to his artistry. “Nimo Live is AraTheJay live on stage. One set at a time, you get to hear AratheJay and listen to his music, but this time you get to feel the individual, get to understand the depth to what he makes music with. It’s not just lyrics and melodies, it’s more than that. That’s why I yearn for the audience to come for Nimo Life, come and experience me more live,” he said. Known for blending traditional Ghanaian Highlife with Afro-soul and contemporary Afrobeats, AratheJay has been spotlighted by Apple Music’s Africa Rising Class of 2025 and Up Next programme, OkayAfrica and Amplify Africa, a testament to his potential to take on the world.

items.title: Le Nobel de littérature attribué à la Canadienne Anne Carson
items.description: Le prix Nobel de littérature 2026 a été décerné jeudi à la poète canadienne Anne Carson, 76 ans, pour son œuvre « audacieuse et inventive » , a annoncé jeudi le jury. L'auteure a été récompensée pour son travail qui « dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a donné naissance à de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine » , a souligné Ingrid Carlberg, secrétaire permanente de l'Académie suédoise. L'Académie suédoise a eu l'occasion d'annoncer rapidement la bonne nouvelle à l'autrice canadienne, qui se trouve en Islande où elle était en train « d'écouter le vent ». Elle est notamment connue pour « Nox » , une œuvre inoubliable, publiée en 2010 en mémoire de son frère Michael, qui avait mystérieusement disparu avant de mourir au Danemark en 2000, explique l'Académie Nobel. L'œuvre se déplie comme une seule longue feuille continue de plusieurs mètres. L'an dernier, l'auteur hongrois László Krasznahorkai a remporté la prestigieuse récompense, pour son œuvre dystopique et mélancolique. Depuis sa création, le Nobel de littérature est dominé par les hommes et les lettres occidentales. Parmi les 123 lauréats, seules 19 femmes ont obtenu le prix et une minorité des auteurs récompensés sont de langues asiatiques ou moyen-orientales. Aucune langue africaine n'est représentée. Le Nobel consiste en un diplôme, une médaille et un chèque de 12 millions de couronnes, soit un peu plus d'un million d'euros. The post Le Nobel de littérature attribué à la Canadienne Anne Carson appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: UBIDS hosts WAC-SRT closing conference as regional partners push for sustainability beyond funding cycle
items.description: The University of Business and Integrated Development Studies (UBIDS) has hosted the International Alumni Meeting and Conference (AMCO) of the West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation (WAC-SRT), bringing together scholars, institutional leaders and alumni from across West Africa and Germany to evaluate the initiative’s impact and map out its future sustainability. The multi-day conference marks the closing chapter of the centre’s primary funding cycle under the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) and the German Federal Foreign Office, which concludes between 2026 and 2027. Officially declaring the conference open at the UBIDS campus in Wa, the Vice-Chancellor of UBIDS and Project Lead for WAC-SRT, Prof. Emmanuel Kanchebe Derbile, revealed that the centre played a foundational role in the operational take-off of UBIDS when the university gained autonomy. “We became a university in 2019 by law, and by May 2020 we had started operations with the constitution of the first-ever Governing Council,” Prof. Derbile stated. “The central administration and many other critical functions or units of this university were supported by the West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation. Many of you may not know that the operations of the central administration for this university started from this centre.” Prof. Derbile highlighted that WAC-SRT was launched on the campus on June 26, 2019, when the institution was still operating as a satellite campus under the University for Development Studies (UDS). He noted that the initiative paved the way for internationalisation in Wa, attracting international postgraduate students from across the sub-region and expanding into cross-border collaborations. To preserve the gains made, Prof. Derbile announced that UBIDS is repositioning the centre within the university’s broader research and grants infrastructure. “We are working to reposition the West African Centre for Sustainable Rural Transformation here at UBIDS as one of the strongest parts of the grantsmanship infrastructure. We are in the process of establishing a Grants Office that would support grantsmanship-related activities, and WAC-SRT comes in handy as part of that infrastructure,” Prof. Derbile noted. He also acknowledged the appointment of Dr. Rudolf Nabogu to the Grants Office and the leadership of the Director of Research, Prof. Frederick Dayour, alongside the WAC-SRT UBIDS Director, Dr. George Dery. Delivering his address, Dr. George Dery underscored that the real impact of the centre extends far beyond the completion of certificates. “WAC-SRT represents much more than a project implemented by a group of institutions. It represents a sustained commitment to building human capacity, strengthening institutions, and generating knowledge for sustainable rural transformation,” Dr. Dery said. “The true value of scholarship cannot be measured only by the number of students supported or degrees completed. Where does the knowledge go? Who benefits from it? What institutions are strengthened?” The Project Coordinator of WAC-SRT and Senior Researcher at the Center for Development Research (ZEF), University of Bonn, Dr. Wolfram Laube, recalled the early stages of establishing the partnership between Anglophone and Francophone institutions, which initially faced mutual scepticism before developing into lasting trust and academic diplomacy. “Beyond the knowledge, beyond the development capacities you may create, there is also this social aspect of collaborating. Meeting each other in person, spending time with each other, seeing each other’s flaws, and seeing each other’s successes is something which I found very valuable in this project,” Dr. Laube remarked. He cautioned that North-South collaborations must remain genuine people-to-people exchanges rather than mere transactions of development assistance. Speaking on behalf of the DAAD Country Director, Ms. Lena Leumer, the Senior Programme Officer at the DAAD Regional Office in Accra, Felix Barnes, assured stakeholders that cooperation would continue through other funding mechanisms. “Funding will be completed by close of 2026/2027, but it’s really the hope that there will be sustainability,” Mr. Barnes noted. “DAAD will not stop there, because there are other avenues of funding that could come in, such as in-country and in-region scholarships. The alumni are certainly our greatest legacy.” Highlighting the programme milestones achieved at the partner campus in Niger, the Academic Assistant of WAC-SRT at Abdou Moumouni University of Niamey (UAM), Dr. Karimoun Massalatchi Illyassou, speaking on behalf of the Dean of the Faculty of Sciences and Techniques, Prof. Bakasso Yacoubou, detailed the cross-border footprint of the initiative. According to Dr. Massalatchi, the centre established the Integrated Master Programme in Sustainable Rural Transformation (EIMP-SRT) in 2018, training eight Master’s cohorts and two PhD cohorts between 2018 and 2026 across engineering and policy tracks. The cohorts comprise students from Niger, Ghana, Mali, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast and Sierra Leone. Adding his voice, the WAC-SRT Coordinator at UDS, Prof. Isaac G.K. Ansah, paid tribute to the four founding architects of the centre: Dr. Wolfram Laube, Prof. Emmanuel Derbile, Prof. Rabani Adamou and Prof. Michael Kpalo, now Deputy CEO of Operations at the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Prof. Ansah challenged the alumni body to maintain active and productive networks. “Let not our alumni network be a WhatsApp group where, on Friday nights, when we are tired, we just send messages. Let’s be an important asset that you can leverage to establish very good relationships that can materialize in the future.” The conference continues with research presentations and gallery walks demonstrating community-level action research interventions across beneficiary West African states.

items.title: FIFA Ranking: Ghana drop five places to 70th following AFCON qualifying defeats
items.description: The Black Stars have fallen to 70th in the latest FIFA Men’s World Ranking following a difficult start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Ghana, previously occupying the 65th position, dropped five places and lost 25.73 points after suffering humble defeats in their opening two qualifying matches, losing 2-0 to Côte d’Ivoire before falling 4-2 to The Gambia. The latest rankings, released on October 7, 2026, were based on 338 men’s international matches played since the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on July 19. These included UEFA and Concacaf Nations League fixtures as well as 2027 AFCON qualifiers. The poor results mark a challenging period for the four-time African champions, who also failed to qualify for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. Following the recent set of defeats, Ghana mutually parted ways with head coach Carlos Queiroz. A scheduled friendly match against Africa’s top-ranked team, Morocco, was also cancelled. Ghana, currently ranked 14th on the African continent, is preparing to rebuild under new management. The Black Stars will look to get back on track in their next international fixture when they face Somalia in back-to-back qualifiers. Somalia is currently ranked 200th in the world. Sitting directly above Ghana in the global standings are the United Arab Emirates in 65th, Albania in 66th, Honduras in 67th, Cabo Verde in 68th, and Jamaica in 69th position, just one place ahead of the Black Stars. Elsewhere in the continent’s standings, Morocco remains Africa’s highest-ranked team at 7th in the world, followed by Senegal in 18th. Côte d’Ivoire sits in 29th, while Nigeria dropped four places to 30th. At the summit of the global standings, the 2026 FIFA World Cup champions, Spain, remain top of the world ranking, with runner-up Argentina second and France third.

items.title: No rift between Agric and Finance Ministries — Eric Opoku dispels rumours
items.description: The Minister of Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku, has dismissed reports of disagreements between his Ministry and the Ministry of Finance, saying both institutions remain committed to advancing the government’s Reset Agenda. According to him, while misunderstandings and miscommunication may occur between institutions, it should not be interpreted as evidence that one ministry is working against another. Speaking at a press briefing in Accra, Mr Opoku said the two ministries are working towards the same national development objectives. “We are working to actualise the same agenda. The Reset Agenda introduced by His Excellency President Mahama,” he said. The Minister acknowledged that misunderstandings can occur, even within families and smaller groups, but said such situations do not mean the parties are working separately. “You know even in our families, in our small circles, misunderstandings and miscommunications do occur. That never suggests that we are doing separatists. We are working together to actualise the Reset Agenda,” he said. Mr Opoku therefore urged the public not to create the impression that some government ministries are working against others. “Let us not create that erroneous impression that other ministries are working against some ministries,” he added. Government rules out total rice import ban On rice imports, Mr Opoku has also ruled out a total ban, saying domestic production currently accounts for about 56 percent of Ghana’s total rice demand. He said the remaining 44 percent supply gap would have to be met through imports while government works towards achieving rice self-sufficiency by 2028. The Minister explained that Ghana imports food because domestic production is currently insufficient to meet demand. “We import food because we are unable to produce. If tomorrow we are able to produce what we eat sufficiently, what is the essence of going to import food again? It doesn’t make sense. So we import what we cannot produce,” he said. Mr Opoku said the government’s approach is therefore to regulate imports rather than impose a complete ban. “So we must import only the 44 percent. And we need to ensure that importation is regulated. It is not about banning,” he said. He reiterated that the government’s ultimate objective is to achieve self-sufficiency in rice production by 2028.

items.title: BRICS: Jinapor cautions Ghana against ‘free lunch’ as NPP demands scrutiny
items.description: Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has cautioned the government to carefully assess the potential risks and benefits of Ghana’s decision to join BRICS, warning that the move could have implications for the country’s national interests. The Damongo MP said while membership of the emerging economic bloc could provide Ghana with new opportunities, including access to funding and diversified international partnerships, the country must not assume that the benefits would come without consequences. His comments come after Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced that Cabinet had approved Ghana’s decision to formally apply to join BRICS, as part of efforts to diversify the country’s international partnerships and deepen South-South cooperation. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show, Mr Jinapor said Ghana’s foreign policy must first and foremost serve the country’s national interest. “All foreign policy must be near to national interests. So there’s absolutely no benefit in a foreign policy move if it does not inure to the national interest of a particular country.” He acknowledged that joining BRICS could offer Ghana important benefits, particularly by expanding its partnerships beyond traditional allies. However, he insisted that the possible implications of the decision must be thoroughly examined. “There’s absolutely no free lunch,” he said. ‘What is the implication?’ Mr Jinapor said the government’s argument that BRICS membership could open up new sources of funding, particularly through the New Development Bank (NDB), required further scrutiny. He questioned whether Ghana would actually gain significant financial independence if access to such funding came with conditions involving existing international institutions. “We are told that we may be in a position to source some new funding from the New Development Bank of BRICS,” he said. “But we are also told that even to access funding from that bank, there’s a condition precedent that the IMF has to give authorisation. So if that is the case, what is the implication?” The former Lands and Natural Resources Minister said Parliament must also examine the possible impact of increased economic and political influence from major BRICS countries such as China and Russia. He said questions surrounding the extent of Chinese influence on Ghana’s economy and national life, as well as the implications of closer relations with Russia, should form part of the assessment. Ethiopia’s experience Mr Jinapor further urged the government to study the experiences of countries that have already joined BRICS before Ghana proceeds with its application. He cited Ethiopia as an example, saying its experience had produced both benefits and challenges. According to him, Ethiopia had benefited from assistance and funding opportunities through the New Development Bank but had also faced concerns over its trade imbalance and increased imports from BRICS countries, particularly China. “We need to take a look at what has been the experience of some of those countries which have joined,” he said. He argued that Ghana could learn valuable lessons by examining how membership has affected the economies and international relationships of the countries that have already joined the bloc. BRICS currently has 11 full members, including Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. South Africa relationship Mr Jinapor also questioned how Ghana’s existing relationship with South Africa could affect its participation in the bloc. South Africa is one of the founding members of BRICS, but the MP said Ghana’s bilateral relationship with the country was currently poor. “Our bilateral relationship with South Africa is almost at the bottom’s end,” he said. He therefore argued that the government must consider what the current state of Ghana-South Africa relations could mean for Ghana’s participation in a grouping in which Pretoria remains an important player. ‘We need a lot more reflection’ Mr Jinapor said Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee had only received a general briefing from the Foreign Affairs Minister on the government’s intention to pursue BRICS membership and had yet to fully interrogate the decision. “We need a lot more reflection on this particular move,” he said. He acknowledged the government’s stated objective of diversifying Ghana’s international partnerships and strengthening cooperation with developing countries. However, he stressed that Ghana’s long-standing policy of non-alignment must also be considered. “It is all good to diversify our partnerships, but without doubt, this will come with some implications as well, some of which may be adverse to our national interest as a country,” Mr Jinapor said. The government says the BRICS bid is intended to give Ghana greater options for development financing, trade, investment and industrialisation while complementing, rather than replacing, its existing relationships with traditional development partners.

items.title: Medical SOS by AMS coordonne une évacuation sanitaire en haute mer au large de Conakry
items.description: Conakry, République de Guinée ─ Medical SOS by AMS a récemment coordonné une évacuation sanitaire complexe en haute mer pour un patient se trouvant à bord d’un porte-conteneurs au large des côtes guinéennes. De l’intervention maritime jusqu’à l’hospitalisation à la Clinique Pasteur de Conakry, puis au transfert international vers l’Europe, les équipes ont assuré une chaîne de prise en charge continue, adaptée aux contraintes de chaque étape. Une intervention médicale dans un environnement complexe Lorsqu’une urgence médicale survient en pleine mer, l’accès au patient et son transfert vers une structure de soins nécessitent une coordination étroite entre les équipes médicales, maritimes et logistiques. Dans cette situation, la configuration du porte-conteneurs ne permettait pas un transfert classique. Une opération spécifique a donc été organisée pour permettre la descente du patient par grue depuis le navire vers une corvette, avant son transfert par voie maritime jusqu’à Conakry. Chaque étape a été préparée afin de limiter les ruptures de prise en charge et d’assurer le transfert dans des conditions adaptées à son état. De la haute mer à l’hôpital : assurer la continuité des soins À son arrivée à Conakry, le patient a été pris en charge, puis hospitalisé à la Clinique Pasteur afin de bénéficier des examens et soins nécessaires. Dans ce type d’intervention, l’enjeu ne se limite pas à extraire un patient d’un environnement difficile d’accès. Il s’agit d’organiser une véritable chaîne de soins : préparation du transfert, coordination maritime, accueil à terre, transport vers l’établissement de santé et transmission des informations médicales aux équipes d’accueil. Cette organisation permet de maintenir la continuité de la prise en charge d’un patient en état critique tout au long du parcours et d’adapter les moyens mobilisés à l’évolution de la situation médicale. Une prise en charge poursuivie jusqu’en Europe À l’issue de son hospitalisation en réanimation à la Clinique Pasteur de Conakry, le patient nécessitait la poursuite de soins spécialisés. Medical SOS by AMS a alors programmé son évacuation sanitaire internationale, en coordination avec le réseau assurantiel, vers son pays d’origine en Europe. Cette dernière étape a nécessité une nouvelle coordination entre les équipes médicales, les acteurs du transport et la structure de destination afin d’assurer la continuité du parcours de soins au-delà de la Guinée. Une expertise issue de plus de 20 ans d’expérience sur le terrain Cette opération illustre la capacité de Medical SOS by AMS à intervenir dans des contextes complexes et à coordonner des évacuations sanitaires de bout en bout. Cette expertise s’inscrit dans l’expérience développée par AMS depuis plus de 20 ans auprès des sites industriels et miniers en Guinée, où la gestion des urgences, l’anticipation des risques et la continuité des soins constituent des exigences quotidiennes. Aujourd’hui, Medical SOS met cette expérience au service des entreprises, organisations et particuliers, avec une capacité de coordination médicale 24h/24 pour les situations critiques, en Guinée comme à l’international. Une chaîne de soins coordonnée de bout en bout Une évacuation sanitaire ne se résume pas à un transport. Elle repose sur la capacité à évaluer la situation, mobiliser les bons interlocuteurs, anticiper les contraintes du terrain et coordonner chaque étape jusqu’à la structure de destination. De la prise en charge en haute mer au transfert vers Conakry, puis à l’évacuation internationale vers l’Europe, cette intervention reflète l’approche de Medical SOS by AMS : une réponse médicale structurée, réactive et coordonnée, centrée sur la sécurité du patient et la continuité des soins. items.title: Bono East Education Directorate invites basic school teachers for SHS/SHTS reposting
items.description: The Bono East Regional Education Directorate has opened an opportunity for suitably qualified professional teachers currently teaching at the basic school level to express interest in being reposted to selected Senior High Schools and Senior High Technical Schools (SHS/SHTS) across the region. According to a press release issued on Thursday, September 29, the initiative is aimed at addressing existing subject-teaching vacancies in schools where the services of qualified teachers are required. According to the Directorate, interested teachers must possess the relevant subject knowledge, academic background, professional competence, and teaching experience necessary to effectively teach at the SHS/SHTS level. Subjects with vacancies The areas in which teachers are being sought include: Visual Arts Home Economics (Food and Nutrition) Economics Clothing and Textiles Social Studies English Language Literature in English Wood Technology Physics Biology Chemistry Electricals/Electrical Technology Government Geography Graphic Design Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Christian Religious Studies (CRS) General Science Ghanaian Language (Asante Twi) Business Management Application process Teachers interested in the reposting opportunity are required to submit an application letter, together with copies of their relevant academic and professional certificates. Applications should be addressed to: The Regional Director Bono East Regional Education Office Post Office Box 50 Nkronza – B/E The Directorate has urged interested teachers to submit their documents to the appropriate office no later than Wednesday, October 21. The opportunity is specifically targeted at professional teachers currently serving in basic schools who meet the required academic and professional standards for teaching at the SHS/SHTS level. Teachers seeking consideration are therefore encouraged to ensure that their applications and supporting documents are submitted before the stated deadline.

items.title: L'Algérie remet au Maroc 33 ressortissants via le poste-frontière de Zouj Beghal
items.description: Les autorités algériennes ont remis, ce mercredi 7 octobre 2026, une nouvelle vague de 33 ressortissants marocains aux autorités du pays au niveau du poste-frontière de Zouj Beghal, à une quinzaine de kilomètres de la ville d'Oujda. Les personnes concernées faisaient l'objet de mesures de détention ou d'arrestation en Algérie dans le cadre de dossiers liés à l'immigration irrégulière. Selon les données communiquées par l'Association marocaine d'aide aux migrants en situation difficile, le groupe comprend un mineur qui a immédiatement été remis à sa famille par les services compétents. La majorité de ces ressortissants est originaire de la région de Ksar El Kébir, tandis que les autres proviennent de diverses villes du Royaume, notamment Nador, Settat, Oujda, Fès, Berkane, Taounate, Casablanca, Taza, Errachidia, Tinghir, Tétouan et Jerada. Cette opération a donné lieu à des scènes de retrouvailles poignantes à Oujda, où de nombreuses personnes et des mères de famille se sont rassemblées au niveau de la place de la Poste pour accueillir leurs proches à leur retour sur le sol national. L'Association marocaine d'aide aux migrants en situation difficile indique qu'elle continue de suivre plusieurs autres dossiers d'acteurs de la migration, incluant des Marocains toujours détenus ou arrêtés, ainsi que des cas de personnes portées disparues ou décédées. Cette action d'accompagnement comprend la présence lors de certaines procédures judiciaires et l'aide à la constitution et à l'envoi de documents administratifs pour établir l'identité ou les liens de parenté des personnes concernées. Dans ce même contexte, l'organisation suit de près l'évolution du dossier du jeune Yassine Dzaz, tout en exprimant sa préoccupation grandissante face au sort de plusieurs Marocains retenus ou arrêtés en Libye. L'association précise que la mise en œuvre de son programme d'accompagnement et de soutien entraîne une sollicitation accrue de la part des familles en quête d'assistance et de suivi pour leurs proches en difficulté. The post L'Algérie remet au Maroc 33 ressortissants via le poste-frontière de Zouj Beghal appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Wa West MP commissions education and health infrastructure projects across rural communities
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Wa West, Peter Lanchene Toobu, alongside officials of the Wa West District Assembly, has commissioned and handed over several completed educational and health infrastructure projects across rural communities in the district. The tour covered projects at Varempere, Gombile and Dabo, and concluded with a grand durbar at Pase. The completed infrastructure includes a six-unit primary classroom block at Varempere, a long-stalled Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compound at Gombile, a Junior High School (JHS) block at Dabo, and a modern CHPS compound with residential staff quarters at Pase. Addressing the durbars, Peter Lanchene Toobu highlighted the principle of continuity in public administration, arguing that changes in government must never justify the abandonment of taxpayer-funded infrastructure. “We don’t really care whether a project was started by President Kufuor or President Nana Akufo-Addo. As long as it was meant for the people and funded by the state, it must not be abandoned,” Toobu stated. “Democracy should not be reduced to voting alone; the true essence of governance lies in the tangible developments brought to communities between elections.” At Varempere Primary School, the commissioning of the six-unit classroom block addressed long-standing infrastructure deficits. The MP also handed over 50 plastic chairs to support early childhood education and promised additional furniture. The District Director of Education, Seidu Kassim, handed the keys to community leaders and urged them to protect the investment. “This building is now in the hands of Varempere. Let us embrace a culture of maintenance so that we do not return here to find broken fixtures and hanging windows,” Mr Kassim said. PTA Chairman Bayor Adams thanked the MP and the Assembly, pledging that parents and teachers would take care of the facility. At Dabo, where a modern JHS block was commissioned, the MP warned contractors against delivering substandard work, noting that an earlier school block constructed in 2006 had deteriorated within four years. Dabo JHS students expressed their excitement about the new facility. Bonle Bernice said: “Previously, moving motorbikes and pedestrians distracted us because our classroom lacked doors and windows. Now, we have a quiet and secure place to learn, and we promise to study hard and score single-digit aggregates.” Another pupil, Ganiu Misbawu, welcomed the new structure but appealed for additional teachers to help students prepare for the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE). Bultou Naa, Naa Touganle M. Philip, who spoke on behalf of the representative of the Dabo Naa, commended the MP and the Assembly while requesting the electrification of the school to support ICT learning. He also appealed for a modern community market and the establishment of a technical Senior High School. The commissioning tour also significantly improved access to healthcare for residents in Gombile and Pase. At Gombile, where a CHPS compound that was started in 2019 was revived and completed with legacy funds from the District Assemblies Common Fund, community elder Dole Naa, Naa Iddrisu Lala, known as “Nansaldau”, said the facility would help prevent maternal emergencies. “When a woman goes into labour in the middle of the night, transporting her over rough roads on a motorbike has always been dangerous. This facility brings dignity and safety to our mothers and wives,” he stated. The MP assured residents that the Gombile CHPS compound would soon be connected to the government’s off-grid solar programme. At the grand durbar in Pase, Kong Naa, Naa Yendau Dong Issac, commended the initiative and called for united community support to maintain the clinic so it could eventually be expanded into a full health centre. The Assembly Member for the Dorimon Electoral Area, Fuseini Saaka, also commended the Assembly and the MP. He explained that Pase initially had a community-initiated health outpost before the Assembly intervened to construct the permanent and fully furnished CHPS facility. He noted that neighbouring communities, including Guo, Kong and Kondoni, would directly benefit from the facility, sparing residents the need to travel long distances to Dorimon to access healthcare. Mr Saaka pledged that the community would recruit a security guard and cleaner. He also made two specific appeals. “We appeal to the authorities to post a midwife here to assist the nurse and ensure safer deliveries for our pregnant women. Furthermore, Dorimon is central to our traditional area, and the current health centre is no longer adequate; we urgently appeal for it to be upgraded into a polyclinic.” The Wa West District Health Director, Cecilia Kakariba, described the Pase facility as “hope and life for rural people”, highlighting that the inclusion of staff quarters would end the reliance on intermittent outreach visits. Ms Kakariba appealed for additional equipment and services to make the clinic fully operational. “To provide comprehensive service, we urgently need a dedicated motorbike for the nurse to collect drugs from Wechiau and carry out outreach, electricity and water connections, and a solar vaccine refrigerator to safely store critical vaccines and medicines,” she said. She also warned residents against neglecting the security of health workers, noting that previous security lapses in the district had forced the withdrawal of some health workers. Representing the District Chief Executive, the Deputy Coordinating Director of the Wa West District Assembly, Martin K. Berisie, noted that the Assembly had earlier commissioned an institutional guest house and provided furniture in Wechiau, alongside other projects at Tanina, Dodoma and Metii. “So, development is a shared responsibility. While the government is providing the resources, the Assembly is providing the technical know-how, the MP is providing or lobbying for more development projects for the district, and the traditional authorities are also releasing the land for us to construct these projects,” Mr Berisie said.

items.title: Quand la calèche devient l’unique issue
items.description: Face aux inondations persistantes qui paralysent certaines parties de Dakar au lendemain des fortes averses, notamment la Zone de captage et Grand Yoff, les véhicules hippomobiles s'imposent comme une alternative pour les piétons bloqués. Entre soulagement des usagers et flambée subite des tarifs de traversée, ces transports de fortune rythment par ces temps le quotidien d'une population dakaroise éprouvée. Le lundi 5 octobre 2026, il est 12 h 30 à la Zone de captage de la commune de Grand Yoff. Au lendemain des fortes pluies tombées sur la capitale, les stigmates des intempéries marquent encore tout ce quartier. Le décor est amer : les accumulations d’eau s'étalent largement sur la chaussée et les rues reliant les différentes parties du quartier immobilisent plusieurs véhicules. Les habitations situées à proximité de cet axe sont, pour la plupart, cernées par les flots et les routes se retrouvent coupées. Sur les passages les plus délicats, les voitures se font rares ; là où elles hésitent à s’engager, les attelages prennent le relais. Sur cette artère difficilement praticable, située à côté du bassin de rétention, les passants n’ont guère le choix. Pour rejoindre l’autre rive, certains pataugent, tandis que d’autres guettent un moyen de locomotion. Les charrettes offrent alors une alternative salvatrice aux usagers. Venus combler ce déficit, les cochers profitent bien de la situation. Ici, pour passer d’un côté à l’autre, il faut débourser au moins 200 FCfa. Mais, les prix pratiqués ne font pas l’unanimité, même chez les cochers eux-mêmes. Pendant qu’un rabatteur essaie d’organiser l’ordre, un charretier débarque et réclame soudainement 500 FCfa. Le régulateur, l’air surpris, l’interpelle aussitôt : « Tu dois respecter le tarif appliqué ici ». Le propriétaire de l’attelage ne cède pas. « Ce n’est pas à toi de me dire ce que je dois faire. Personne ne peut me fixer un prix », martèle-t-il. L’échange attire l’attention. Assise sur une autre charrette, une dame qui suit la scène intervient à son tour. Pour elle, le marché s’autorégulera : « En tout cas, c’est facile à régler. S’il est le seul à appliquer ce tarif, aucun client n’ira vers lui ». La remarque déclenche un éclat de rire général. Le conducteur, quant à lui, campé sur sa position, ne baisse pas la garde. Cheikh Mbaye, un autre professionnel présent sur les lieux, comprend pourtant la tentation de certains collègues d’augmenter leurs exigences financières. Franchir une zone inondée comporte des risques, rappelle-t-il. A l’en croire, l’équipage peut avancer sur plusieurs mètres avant de se retrouver face à un bourbier impraticable, obligeant le cocher à rebrousser chemin ou à modifier son itinéraire. À cela s’ajoutent les charges quotidiennes liées à l’entretien et à l’alimentation du cheval. Aïcha Ndiaye (nom d’emprunt) hésite plusieurs minutes devant les eaux avant de se décider. Ayant commencé d’abord à patauger, elle est vite rattrapée par la réalité des lieux. Elle lâche : « C’est difficile de traverser à pied. C’est sale et ce n’est pas sûr ». Aïcha finit par emprunter elle aussi une charrette, mais la mine triste, elle fulmine : « Payer 200 à 300 FCfa à chaque passage toute la journée, c'est difficile. Surtout que l’eau est partout. Là où on marchait facilement sans problème, il faut dépenser 1000 FCfa ou plus par jour après chaque forte pluie. Je dois aller à Castor et la voie est obstruée ». Le long de cette même voie, l'animation ne faiblit pas. Massamba Guèye, vêtu entièrement de noir, explique comment l'activité s'adapte aux intempéries : « En temps normal, on stationne devant les magasins pour transporter les marchandises et les bagages des clients. Après les averses, on change de route et on vient ici pour acheminer les personnes. On reste sur place jusqu’au reflux des eaux ». Les charretiers se frottent les mains À Grand Yoff, la situation est identique. Les charrettes font des va-et-vient entre la station Patte d’Oie et l’église de Grand Yoff, toutes deux submergées par les eaux. Installé sur sa calèche décorée, Aliou Mar attend la clientèle au milieu des flaques. Une femme s’approche avec un enfant et un gros sac. Visiblement à bout de forces, elle exprime son découragement : « Je n’ai pas le temps, je viens du village et je suis déjà trop épuisée ». Elle tente de monter, mais éprouve quelques difficultés. Aliou lui tend alors la main pour l’aider à prendre place. Le trajet lui revient finalement à 400 FCfa en raison de son chargement. Souleymane Faye s’approche à son tour. Interpellé, il trouve le temps de plaisanter : « Je suis de mère peule et de père sérère. Donc, un vrai mélange ! » Derrière l’humour, la situation est loin d’être anodine. Il explique que progresser à pied signifie prendre le risque de se retrouver complètement trempé. « Mieux vaut prendre une charrette, même si les prix sont souvent élevés pour une si courte distance », avoue-t-il. Interrogés sur les gains réalisés durant ces épisodes pluvieux, les charretiers semblent esquiver la question. Aliou Mar se montre d'abord discret, avant de lâcher dans un sourire : « On se frotte bien les mains ». Soudain, son cheval s'agite et esquisse un pas de côté. Le cocher retient les rênes d'un geste machinal avant de reprendre, le regard fixé sur l'horizon inondé : « Après la pluie, On fait la navette toute la journée, et e, jusqu’à ce que les eaux se retirent définitivement ». Par Ameth NIASS (Stagiaire)

items.title: The Marriage That Captures a High Point of American Art
items.description: C reativity in the context of marriage is a fraught and fascinating subject. The Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York is not the first major show devoted to a married couple. Previous exhibits have featured, among others, Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, Georgia O’Keeffe and Alfred Stieglitz, and Sonia and Robert Delaunay. But the Met, as only the Met can, has given “Krasner and Pollock: Continuous Present” the full blockbuster treatment: stupendous loans, beautiful installation, a narrative both compelling and cleanly told. Better yet, it does each artist the honor of representing them at their best. The exhibition establishes beyond a doubt what many in the art world have long mumbled but few have avowed full-throatedly: that Krasner (1908–84) was not only more richly endowed with training and talent, but was as accomplished and original as her more famous husband. It also makes a powerful case, through their partnership, for abstract expressionism as an unassailable peak of 20th-century American visual expression. Unlike Pollock (1912–56), a tormented and recalcitrant misfit, Krasner was a go-getter from the start. She received the best possible education at some of New York’s finest art schools. She benefited from practical training in large-scale mural painting under the Works Progress Administration in the 1930s and three years of training in modernism under Hans Hofmann, the émigré teacher versed in Matisse, Mondrian, and Kandinsky. Krasner could draw; she could manipulate paint; she could work on any scale—and she was modern. Her great period—roughly from ’57 to ’65, with an exciting burst again in the early ’70s—came late and was regrettably brief. But during these peak years, she produced a series of tremendous, richly colored paintings, several of which—including Polar Stampede , Combat , and The Seasons —look better to me than anything painted by her contemporaries. What’s dismaying is that, having found her way to a triumphant new mode of painting, she turned out so few of these works. Was something holding her back? Whitney Museum of American Art, Purchase with funds from Frances and Sydney Lewis by exchange, the Mrs. Percy Uris Purchase Fund and the Painting and Sculpture Committee. Lee Krasner, The Seasons, 1957. No single reason can ever explain why creativity flows, slows, or stops. But yes, something was holding her back. And it was the same thing that had helped push her forward. It was the brute fact of her marriage to Jackson Pollock. T ogether, Krasner and Pollock represent a high point of 20th-century American art. No one had ever made abstract paintings in this way, on this scale, and with this level of visceral impact. The rhetoric about the abstract expressionists was, from the beginning, absurdly grandiose. “What was to go on the canvas was not a picture,” wrote the critic Harold Rosenberg in “The American Action Painters,” a key essay from 1952, “but an event.” The movement, though, is best understood in terms of energy. Standing in front of a great Pollock or Krasner is thrilling. You can almost feel air moving at a frightening velocity through and around the forms on the canvas. (I had the sensation, in the middle parts of this show, of sticking my head out of a car window on an interstate highway and an accompanying urge to shout stupid things at the universe.) The wind coursing through Krasner’s paintings is terrestrial. It brushes the contours of hills and bodies. It rustles the branches of tropical foliage and long winter grasses. The wind generated by Pollock, by contrast, is celestial, like solar wind. Its charged particles are sparsely scattered but fast, frictionless, inhumanly distant. Never more than an earnest draftsman, Pollock had labored for years to synthesize disparate influences, both spiritual and artistic. Schooled in the complex figurative compositions of his mentor, the regionalist Thomas Hart Benton, he grew to love the scale and political urgency of the Mexican muralists (especially David Alfaro Siqueiros, who encouraged technical experimentation); the surrealism of Joan Miró, André Masson, and Roberto Matta; and the totems and sand painting of Native American art. In 1947, Pollock hit upon an ingenious new method: Laying his canvases on the studio floor, he moved around them, dripping liquid enamel paint in loose, spattery patterns by means of a brush, stick, or turkey baster that he waved about like a wand. [ Read: The artist who ripped up the rules of drawing ] He did this with surprising delicacy and a preternatural feeling for the space between things. He adopted an “allover” approach that dissolved distinctions between figure and background and did away with compositional hierarchy, implying infinite expansion in every direction. People either adore Pollock or claim that a child could do just as well. But his method entails more artfulness than his detractors are willing to acknowledge. There’s also a lot of chance involved. Although Pollock’s skeins of paint are like traces of an energetic dance, they are as much the product of gravity as of a painter’s direct touch, and they incline toward decoration. (The painter Francis Bacon rather devastatingly compared them to “tired old lace.”) For all of the energy they record, the paintings are surprisingly calm, in the same way that stars, those giant balls of hot gas and plasma, can seem tranquil in the night sky. Chromatically, the overall impact is of soft, atomized color (as captured in the title of one of his masterpieces, Lavender Mist ) twinkling through a scrim of black, beige, and white. National Gallery of Art / Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund / 2026 Pollock-Krasner Foundation / Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York. Jackson Pollock, Lavender Mist: Number 1, 1950. Krasner, by contrast, worked with large areas of saturated color. She painted with big arm gestures, applying bright hues directly to upright canvases. She also flicked and sprayed paint, letting it explode diagonally across her surfaces, often against gravity. She combined her rich repertoire of painterly effects with confidently drawn armatures that set giant curves in tension with acute-angled shards. Her muscular compositions are tremendously dynamic. The forms are abstract, but they suggest eyes, body parts, fruits, foliage, rolling landscapes. No artist has more successfully combined the shallow pictorial space of Picasso and Braque (who dissolved the boundaries separating “figure” from “background”) and the saturated color of late Matisse (especially his cutouts). Abstract expressionism was the product of a moment, during and after World War II, when the West’s center of gravity shifted—militarily, economically, and culturally—from Europe to North America, and the art world’s center moved from Paris to New York. The movement was fueled by émigrés, but it was unmistakably American. A measure of its impact is that almost every major artist who came after Pollock, Krasner, and other prominent abstract expressionists was somehow engaged with them. Whether they amplified abstract expressionism, ironized it, or rejected it, succeeding generations of artists were all, to some degree, operating in its force field. [ Read: The irrepressible emotion of Lee Krasner ] It wasn’t just artists. Dancers, performance artists, and composers also drew from this force field, and so did writers. In an interview with David Remnick, Philip Roth once said that in his late novels, he had tried “to cover every square inch with real stuff” in the same way that Pollock had “dramatized” every square inch of his paintings. Marriage is also a force field, a weather system, formed by shifts in pressure and sometimes giant displacements of energy. Krasner and Pollock met in 1941. They both had been chosen to present their work in an exhibition organized by the Ukrainian émigré John Graham and dominated by European modernists, including Picasso, Matisse, Modigliani, and Bonnard. San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, Albert M. Bender Collection / 2026 Pollock-Krasner Foundation / Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York. Jackson Pollock, Guardians of the Secret, 1943. Pollock was the younger brother of a successful painter, Charles Pollock. Krasner found him handsome and echt -American (she was the daughter of Russian Jewish immigrants). Yes, he was troubled—but she felt she could handle him. She might have been right. But the more pertinent question soon became: Could he handle the success that she had helped him achieve? She had supported him in staying sober for several years. But when word of his breakthrough spread, he became more famous than any American painter before him. He was unprepared for so much notoriety. “I feel like a clam without a shell,” he once said. He also felt like an imposter. Pollock tried to go beyond the drip method, which was on one hand a grand manner but, on the other, a slender achievement by a man of narrow talents. Yet his attempts spluttered and failed, his drinking got out of hand, his former champions abandoned him, and he began to unravel. T he premise of the Met show is that Krasner’s and Pollock’s works “cannot be understood in singularity, but only in relation to each other.” This strikes me as an unnecessarily deterministic position to take. (Must we always think of Diego Rivera when looking at Frida Kahlo?) But even as they emphasize the intertwined nature of Pollock’s and Krasner’s creativity, the exhibit’s curators, David Breslin and Brinda Kumar, in their catalog introduction, want us to distinguish between biographical interpretations (how did the conditions of the marriage affect what was made?) and artistic influence (how did the paintings of one affect those of the other?). The show is so deftly and intelligently installed that you need only to open your eyes to see how closely each artist looked at the other’s work, and how such close looking stimulated further innovations. But Breslin and Kumar caution against dwelling too much on biography. Biography “is not enough to understand a person,” they correctly contend. “As closely as we may attempt to approach the historical figures we study, we can never close the door and be truly alone with them and those they love.” Their introduction concludes with the assertion, “Like love, we don’t need to know what or why it is as long as we feel it.” This is where I rebel. The “what” and “why” of biography really do matter in the case of Krasner and Pollock. Moreover, there’s more to a marriage than love. National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne, Felton Bequest, 1992 / 2026 Pollock-Krasner Foundation / Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York. Lee Krasner, Combat, 1965. Think about it: Pollock made his big breakthrough after he and Krasner had moved to Springs, East Hampton. They would not have moved to Long Island—away from all of the dynamism of downtown New York and the scene Krasner had done so much to cultivate—had she not realized that she needed to remove Pollock from easy access to alcohol. They moved into a farmhouse, and Pollock soon got to work in a big barn tailored to his needs, while Krasner painted in the house’s upstairs bedroom. This—the “what” and the “why”—explains the reason that, during this period, Pollock’s paintings were so big and Krasner’s were so small. Krasner’s paintings became big, and she entered her great period, only in 1957, when she moved her things into the barn. She could do this because, in 1956, Pollock ended his drawn-out, slow-motion decline by getting drunk and taking Ruth Kligman, the younger woman for whom he had recently abandoned Krasner, for a spin in his car, which he plowed into a tree, killing himself and Kligman’s friend, Edith Metzger. Krasner’s creative output was affected, in other words, not just at the aesthetic level but at every other level by her marriage to Pollock. We wouldn’t have this understanding were it not for the flawed project we call biography. What we learn from biography is often unpleasant, even embarrassingly melodramatic, but we shouldn’t affect so much white-gloved urbanity as to find it distasteful. T he Pollock-Krasner marriage was not a marriage of equals. It was unequal, primarily because Pollock was weak and Krasner was strong. Pollock had a sweet and charismatic side, and Krasner definitely fell hard for him. But he was also insecure, chaotic, and bullying. Plagued by alcoholism, he hurt not only Krasner but others in their orbit too. Krasner used her personal strength to shelter her husband and tend to his needs. She created an environment where he could feel good about himself and paint freely. Her strength came into play after his death, too, when she dedicated time and energy to managing his reputation, at the expense of her own creative output. His fame, and the explosion of the postwar art market, made this a full-time undertaking, surely made bitter by everyone’s knowledge that her husband had died in a car with his younger lover (who survived and of course wrote a memoir, Love Affair ). Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Eugene Victor Thaw, 1983 / 2026 Pollock-Krasner Foundation / Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York. Lee Krasner, Rising Green , 1972. The Pollock-Krasner marriage was also unequal for the obvious reason that she was a woman and he was a man. In the 1940s and ’50s, as Robert Hughes wrote in a review of a 1983 Krasner show for Time magazine, “the ruling assumptions about the inherent weakness, derivativeness and silly femininity of women painters were almost unbelievably phallocentric.” Krasner’s innate toughness meant she never played the victim. Mary Gabriel’s 2018 book, Ninth Street Women , reveals in detail just how much she, along with Elaine de Kooning, Joan Mitchell, Grace Hartigan, and Helen Frankenthaler did to break down the entrenched chauvinism of the mid-century art world. For Krasner, nonetheless, being married to Pollock meant being relegated to second place. Was Pollock more than a one-hit wonder? This show suggests otherwise. A gallery devoted to the paintings he made from 1942 to ’46 makes it easy to see why Krasner was so convinced of his genius. Something powerful is brewing in these works, which combine lively texture, bright color, and sporadic bursts of calligraphy. They led right into the drip-painting breakthrough. But even as you admire the lacy skeins of volatilized paint that cover the surfaces of Pollock’s thrilling, mythic canvases, you can sense the expressive limitations of his manner. While he was still alive, Krasner, for her part, cycled through a number of styles that emulated her husband’s pattern-based, allover compositions, though on a much smaller scale. Then, in 1955, under the spell of Matisse’s cutouts, she made a series of bright, large-scale collages, slicing up old drawings (hers and his) and placing them over painted grounds. These were exhibited at the Stable Gallery—only her second solo show—and they helped her generate the extraordinary synthesis of form and color, of Picasso, Matisse, and Pollock, that constitutes the paintings she made in her great period. These, to reiterate, are the ones she began after moving into Pollock’s studio and making it her own.

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Building new revenue streams
items.description: Insight. Revenue diversification can strengthen an organisation’s resilience and create new avenues for growth. CEOs should examine whether existing capabilities, customer relationships, intellectual property, distribution networks, or partnerships can support additional sources of revenue. However, new revenue streams should complement the organisation’s strategy rather than create unnecessary complexity. Key Strategies: Identify assets and capabilities that can create additional value. Examine unmet needs among existing customers. Explore complementary products and services. Assess recurring and scalable revenue opportunities. Establish clear financial and strategic criteria for new ventures. CEO Leadership Actions. Review the organisation’s dependence on its existing revenue sources. Identify at least two credible opportunities for revenue diversification. Require all new revenue initiatives to demonstrate a clear path to customer value and financial sustainability. Actionable Tip. Ask: “What else could we offer our existing customers that solves a meaningful problem and creates additional value?” Why This Matters? A diversified revenue base can provide greater flexibility when market conditions change. The CEO’s responsibility is to ensure that new revenue streams are strategically relevant, financially sound, and manageable within the organisation’s capabilities. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader, and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: Nouvelle alerte pluie en Algérie : jusqu’à 50 mm, 26 wilayas concernées
items.description: Il va pleuvoir ce jeudi et demain vendredi sur plusieurs régions d’Algérie. L’Office national de la météorologie (ONM) a publié un BMS pluie ce jeudi qui annonce des pluies torrentielles dans 26 wilayas du pays. La première alerte de niveau II (orange), valide de ce jeudi 8 octobre à 18 h 00 jusqu’à demain vendredi à 18 h 00, touche Béchar, Béni Abbès et Est de Tindouf, où la quantité de pluie attendue peut atteindre 40 mm. L’ONM a également placé en vigilance orange (niveau II) pluie les wilayas de Tizi Ouzou, Béjaïa, Jijel, Skikda, Annaba, El Tarf, Sétif, Mila, Constantine, Guelma, Souk Ahras, Oum El Bouaghi, Batna, Khenchela et Tébessa, et ce, pendant 24 heures : de ce jeudi 8 octobre (21 h 00) jusqu’à demain vendredi à la même heure. La quantité estimée peut atteindre 50 mm sur les wilayas côtières, selon la même source. Algérie : une fin de semaine pluvieuse dans plusieurs régions Enfin, l’ONM annonce des pluies intenses sur les wilayas de Naâma, Tlemcen, Sidi Bel Abbès, Saïda, Tiaret, Tissemsilt, Médéa et Djelfa, ce jeudi de 12 h 00 à 23 h 00, avec une quantité estimée pouvant atteindre 40 mm. Le retour de la pluie est une bonne nouvelle notamment pour les agriculteurs qui commencent à s’inquiéter du manque d’eau après un été particulièrement chaud. Il survient alors que l’Algérie continue de faire face à des températures caniculaires en pleine automne et que les incendies continuent de ravager les forêts. L’article Nouvelle alerte pluie en Algérie : jusqu’à 50 mm, 26 wilayas concernées est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: ‘Save part of the cake for us’ – Ga Mantse asks Roads Ministry to create jobs quota for Ga indigenes
items.description: The Ga Mantse, Nii Teiko Tsuru II, has appealed to the Roads and Highways Ministry to create a quota for Ga indigenes in employment opportunities within the sector. According to him, reserving opportunities for people from the Ga State would ensure that indigenes benefit directly from development taking place in the capital, which they host. The Ga Mantse made the appeal when Roads and Highways Minister Governs Kwame Agbodza paid a courtesy visit to the Ga Mantse Palace. He said the traditional council was responding to concerns about a reported shortage of workers within the Roads and Highways sector. “We are making a note that you set up a quota for our Ga indigenes to be employed in the various sectors, either engineering or part of your artisan workforce,” he said. Nii Teiko Tsuru II said the arrangement would help ensure that Ga indigenes benefit from opportunities created through development projects in the capital. “It will help us a lot to know that at least part of the cake has been saved for us and the indigenes of this soil who form the host of this capital,” he added. The Ga Mantse also commended the Roads and Highways Minister for what he described as progress on road projects in the Ga State. He said his observations of some of the roads under construction suggest that work is progressing well and expressed confidence that proper supervision and management would help government meet its targets ahead of Ghana’s 70th anniversary next year. “I know that your supervision, attention and good management would let us achieve our targets in due time for next year’s 70th anniversary of our country,” he said. Nii Teiko Tsuru II further called on the Ministry to support the Ga Mantse Foundation, which he said is undertaking several interventions in education, skills development and the welfare of young people. He said the Foundation has supported the construction and refurbishment of schools, provision of sanitation facilities and initiatives aimed at improving the enrolment, retention and academic achievement of girls. The Ga Mantse said the Foundation is also exploring vocational and entrepreneurial skills training to equip young people with skills for employment and self-reliance.
