items.title: Turkiye's FM Fidan says Istanbul assessing aid to Saudi Arabia as part of Makkah agreement
items.description: Turkiye is assessing how it can help Saudi Arabia counter attacks from Yemen’s Houthis under the Makkah defence pact signed between Islamabad, Riyadh and Istanbul, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday. The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. “The technical evaluations are [being] carried out, and these continue among our military officials,” Fidan said during a joint press conference in Ankara with his Hungarian counterpart, adding that officials were working out what contributions could be made, particularly on air defence. Ankara’s top diplomat also stressed that the pact was a defensive agreement, not an offensive one. “When a country of this agreement is attacked, you have to side with them,” Fidan stated. “This is not an attack agreement. Turkiye is not carrying out an attack by sending troops to another country’s land.” The Turkish foreign minister added that the process of sending the text of the agreement to the Turkish parliament for ratification had been finalised. Fidan’s remarks came after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Monday agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh. The emergency meeting of the alliance’s Strategic Political and Defence Committee addressed the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia. “The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” a statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said. While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict. A day prior, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry told CNN that Pakistani troops were already in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has also described the agreement as defensive, without an offensive agenda. Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said Pakistani and Turkish forces would play a supporting role, including reconnaissance, while Saudi forces conduct combat operations.

items.title: L’Italie à l’honneur au BigTech Africa 2026 à Tunis
items.description: L ’ intelligence artificielle, la cybersécurité, le cloud, l ’ innovation industrielle, les startups , les investissements et la coopération technologique seront au cœur de la troisième édition de BigTech Africa, organisé par TPM Events sous le patronage du ministère des Technologies de la communication, qui se tiendra les 13 et 14 octobre 2026 à la Cité de la Culture de Tunis. L’événement se veut une plateforme panafricaine dédiée à la transformation numérique, aux investissements et à la coopération technologique. Selon TPM Events, l’édition 2026 table sur 4 000 participants qualifiés, 100 experts et intervenants, 40 investisseurs internationaux et des représentants de 20 pays, avec un programme comportant un millier de rencontres B2B. Parmi les thèmes abordés figurent l’IA souveraine, la cybersécurité, le cloud africain, la GovTech, la FinTech, la GreenTech, l’Industrie 4.0 ainsi que la confrontation entre l’IA générative et la DeepTech industrielle. L’ICE-Agenzia (Agence italienne pour le commerce extérieur) sera présente avec un «Punto Italia» (Espace Italie) dédié à la promotion de l’écosystème national de l’innovation ; y seront présentées des initiatives telles que Labinnova, Terna Innovation Zone et Innovatech, ainsi que les activités d’incubateurs et d’accélérateurs italiens. Cet espace prévoit également des temps forts consacrés à la formation, au réseautage et à la présentation de projets et de compétences issus du système italien. Le 14 octobre, de 14h25 à 15h25, la scène principale ( «Main Stage » ) accueillera une table ronde intitulée «L ’ Italie comme pont pour l'innovation Italie-Afrique : dialogue entre institutions, innovation en entreprise et écosystème des startups» , modérée par Bernard Prevete, directeur du bureau de l’ICE à Tunis. Parmi les intervenants figurent notamment Paolo Anselmo (président de l’Italian Business Angels Network), Luigi Giorgi (Terna), Marco D’Angelo (InnovUp et beeco), Francesco Gavanna (Fintech District) et Viera Schioppetto (CIES). Le débat portera sur l’établissement de partenariats entre l’Italie et l’Afrique dans les domaines du mentorat, de l’investissement, de l’incubation et du transfert de compétences. Cette présence italienne s’inscrit dans le cadre d’un événement visant à faire de Tunis un carrefour entre les écosystèmes technologiques africains, européens et internationaux, en favorisant la mise en relation d'institutions, d'entreprises, de startups, d'investisseurs et de centres d’innovation. Pour l’Italie, BigTech Africa constitue ainsi une opportunité de renforcer la coopération économique et technologique avec la Tunisie et, plus largement, avec les marchés africains émergents dans le secteur de l’innovation numérique. I. B. L’article L’Italie à l’honneur au BigTech Africa 2026 à Tunis est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: COCOBOD raises GH¢3.4bn in first cocoa notes offer, 15% below indicative GH¢4bn target
items.description: COCOBOD has raised approximately GH¢3.4 billion through its first commercial paper issuance, falling about GH¢604 million short of the indicative GH¢4 billion presented to investors. COCOBOD’s investor presentation The funds were raised through Cocoa Capital PLC, the wholly owned company established by COCOBOD to borrow from investors under its new domestic financing programme. According to the published results, GH¢3.39 billion was allotted at a yield of 11%. The notes were issued on October 5, 2026, and will mature on June 28, 2027. Source: Ghana Stock Exchange The amount represents approximately 85% of the initial GH¢4 billion financing plan for the first tranche. However, the GH¢4 billion was an indicative figure in the investor presentation. That distinction matters because the amount accepted is not necessarily the total amount investors offered. The published results do not state how much COCOBOD received in bids or whether some were rejected. It is therefore unclear whether investors offered less than expected, demanded rates COCOBOD was unwilling to pay, or whether the company decided to raise a smaller amount. The issuance also took place later than initially planned. Cocoa Capital’s September 25 announcement set out an indicative timetable for bidding to close on September 30, followed by settlement and issuance on October 1. The notes were eventually issued on October 5, four calendar days later. Source: Cocoa Capital’s initial announcement Their duration was also reduced from 270 to 266 days. The final yield of 11% was at the upper end of the initial guidance of 10.5% to 11%. These developments raise questions about how readily COCOBOD was able to secure the funds on its preferred terms. But without the full bidding results, they do not explain why it raised less than initially envisaged. The first issuance forms part of a programme allowing up to GH¢16.3 billion in notes to be outstanding at any time. Approximately GH¢14 billion is intended to finance cocoa purchases through commercial paper, while GH¢2.3 billion in longer-term bonds is intended to refinance existing debt. There is also an unresolved question over how the first GH¢3.4 billion will be used. As JoyNews Research previously reported, the investor presentation assigned commercial paper to cocoa purchases. The issuance announcement, however, also listed repayment of a bridge loan obtained to refinance COCOBOD’s legacy debt. Read here: COCOBOD asks investors to fund cocoa purchases, but proceeds may also repay old debt The latest notice does not disclose how much will be used to purchase cocoa and how much, if any, will repay that loan. The prospectus says details of bridge funding should be disclosed in the relevant pricing supplement, the document setting out the terms of each issuance. As of October 8, that document was not available on Cocoa Capital’s website. Meanwhile, COCOBOD has indicated that it could return to the market shortly. Speaking on Channel One TV’s The Point of View on September 28, Deputy Chief Executive in charge of Finance and Administration, Ato Boateng, indicated that COCOBOD could return to the market about two weeks after the first issuance. “Maybe two weeks later… we’ll come in and then do another tranche, and then we’ll finally look at the GH¢2.3 billion, which is the longer term, ” he said. Deputy Cocobod CEO, Ato Boateng His comments suggest that the next round of fundraising could follow shortly. The first offer gives COCOBOD a basis for deciding how much to seek next and at what price. Whether investors will provide more money on similar terms remains to be seen. For now, the amount raised is known. How much investors offered, why COCOBOD accepted less than its initial financing plan, and how the money will be divided between cocoa purchases and debt repayment remain unclear.

items.description: By Simon Johnson and Johan Ahlander STOCKHOLM, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature", the Swedish Academy said on Thursday. "She was very taken by surprise," said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the academy, which awards the prize worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).

items.title: Italia aprueba la controvertida reforma electoral de Meloni y se acerca a unas elecciones anticipadas
items.description: El voto secreto, solicitado por la oposición con la esperanza de que en las filas del Gobierno hubiera alguna rebelión interna, no ha surtido efecto y la Cámara de Diputados italiana ha aprobado a mediodía de este jueves el controvertido cambio del sistema electoral . La ley ha salido adelante con 227 votos a favor y 164 en contra en una sesión en que la oposición ha exhibido carteles que decían “No al embrollo” y “Ley estafa”. La primera ministra, Giorgia Meloni, había amenazado a los suyos con convocar elecciones anticipadas de inmediato si la ley no era aprobada, pues ya en julio hubo al menos 40 votos en su coalición en contra de la norma. La aprobación parlamentaria de la ley, sin embargo, también pavimenta el camino para unos comicios adelantados en cuestión de meses. Seguir leyendo

Dzata Cement proves Ghanaians can build large-scale businesses – Ibrahim Mahama
items.description: Business mogul Ibrahim Mahama has called for greater belief in Ghanaians and urged the state to provide deliberate support to help more local entrepreneurs grow. He stressed that entrepreneurship was not only about creating a successful company, but also ensuring that the enterprise survives its founder. Mr Mahama, who is the Founder, Sole Shareholder and Group Chief Executive Officer of DZATA Holdings, said one of his motivations for establishing Dzata Cement was to demonstrate that Ghanaians could build major businesses rather than remain dependent on foreign-owned enterprises. “There are other ventures in which I want to prove to Ghanaians that we can’t always be beggars and only be employees of foreign companies. We can build it ourselves,” he said last Tuesday at the fifth anniversary celebration of Dzata Cement, a Portland cement production factory in Tema. Mr Mahama said his experiences and achievements in establishing Dzata Cement were a validation of a conviction that Ghanaian entrepreneurs could conceive, finance, build and operate large-scale industrial businesses and create enterprises capable of competing in sectors critical to national development. The only wholly Ghanaian-owned cement manufacturing company, Dzata Cement, marked five years of resilience last Tuesday, showcasing the proof that indigenous companies can thrive in all areas. Mr Mahama weathered significant financial, operational and market challenges to establish the company as a growing and recognised brand in the country’s construction industry. Dzata Cement’s journey, therefore, represents more than the establishment of a manufacturing plant; it is a demonstration of the entrepreneurial vision of the founder of DZATA Holdings, who set out to challenge the long-held perception that large-scale industrial ventures, particularly in the cement industry, had to be built and owned by foreign companies. Five years on, the cement manufacturing operation, located on a 10-acre plot near Tema Port, represents an investment of more than $100 million. The plant uses technology from German equipment developer Haver & Boecker to produce Portland Cement, with bagging lines capable of averaging 120 bags per minute. The company says its current operations have a capacity of about 80,000 bags a day, equivalent to approximately two million tonnes annually. The company is expected to produce its 30 millionth bag of cement within days, providing a significant production milestone in its five years of operations. Mr Mahama also urged those in leadership to challenge younger people with responsibility to help nurture a new generation of “doers who can take over from the current generation. He said he had deliberately stepped away from the day-to-day management of Dzata Cement to give younger leaders the opportunity to take risks, acquire experience and develop their managerial capabilities. “In life, some of us should learn these lessons. We won’t live forever. So sometimes we should give the children the opportunity to be able to take that risk of managing,” he said. Mr Mahama explained his broader succession philosophy: “What we do is that we start running together and then as our children grow, we employ them into the business, we teach them, and then we go into retirement.” That philosophy is already reflected at Dzata, where his daughter, Nafisa Mahama, serves as Managing Director. Mr Mahama traced the origins of Dzata Cement to his days as a cement transporter and mining contractor. His involvement in transporting cement gave him the opportunity to observe the industry closely, including the manufacturing and distribution processes. Mr Mahama recalled following his trucks to the Ghacem facility in Takoradi and taking a closer look at the plant and how cement was produced. Rather than seeing the enterprise as beyond the reach of a Ghanaian entrepreneur, the experience convinced him that he could build a similar facility. “I looked at the structure and said, look, I could build one,” he recalled, saying that resolve became an investment decision. Mr Mahama travelled to Germany, engaged equipment manufacturers and began putting together the financing required to establish the plant. The project, however, was confronted by significant financial and operational difficulties during construction and installation. At a critical stage, the business magnate said his younger brother and other individuals provided support that helped complete the installation of the equipment. Mr Mahama said the difficulties of bringing the project on stream did not derail the vision, but became part of the story of an entrepreneur determined to establish a Ghanaian-owned industrial operation in a highly competitive sector. He paid tribute to distributors who stood by the company during its difficult early period. The challenges included raising funds to clear imported clinker, creating a difficult situation while the business was still trying to establish itself in the market. The distributors, however, rallied around the company and helped it overcome the challenge. “They all joined hands together, the cement came, we allocated it to them, and then Dzata Cement started,” Mr Mahama said. He also acknowledged the support of former Trade and Industry Minister, Alan Kwadwo Kyerematen, during the administration of former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. “Alan, wherever you are, I’m giving you a thumbs up. Thank you very much for standing behind us,” Mr Mahama said. His entrepreneurial journey was also shaped by scepticism from some industry players. Mr Mahama recalled an encounter with an expatriate executive who expressed doubts that a Ghanaian could build a cement plant. He said the comment strengthened his determination to prove the doubters wrong. The Managing Director of Dzata Cement, Nafisa Mahama, said the fifth anniversary was an opportunity to express gratitude to the customers whose confidence had helped the company to reach the milestone. She said Dzata Cement was celebrating the anniversary with a deep sense of appreciation for customers who had believed in the brand and chosen its products for their construction projects. She also thanked distributors, describing them as an essential part of the company’s journey. Ms Mahama acknowledged that some distributors had remained with Dzata Cement even during periods when the company faced significant challenges, helping it build the market presence it enjoys today. She also described the employees as the heart of the company and paid tribute to their dedication, sacrifices and commitment to the business. Ms Mahama pledged that employee welfare would remain a priority as the company entered the next phase of its development. She expressed appreciation to local and international suppliers, GCB Bank, the government, state institutions and the Chamber of Cement Producers for their contributions and support. She pledged management’s commitment to strengthening operations, maintaining the quality of Dzata Cement and improving services to customers and distributors. Ms Mahama said the company would increase investment in its people to ensure that Dzata Cement developed the human capacity required to serve Ghana for generations. Beyond the anniversary, the company has outlined plans to strengthen its manufacturing capacity and market position. Plant Director, Abderrahim Ouahab, said the company’s immediate priorities included expanding its cement portfolio, introducing additional grades and exploring a possible 25kg bag alongside the current 50kg packaging. He said the company would also strengthen its laboratory, increase Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) training, pursue ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards; improve spare-parts and inventory management and deploy artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools in selected operations. A major capital project is the installation of a 300-tonne-per-hour Multi Big Bag Receiver, designed to improve jumbo-bag handling, cement transfer, screening, dust collection and recycling. The company also plans to expand storage capacity to 40,000 tonnes and develop an automated packing facility capable of about 6,000 tonnes a day. The managers said the long-term target was to produce at least three million tonnes of cement annually. The Finance Director, Godfred Barnes, said Dzata Cement’s progress had been built on hard work, sacrifice and resilience, stating that the company had navigated supply-chain disruptions, freight costs, inflation, exchange-rate volatility and operational pressures. He said finance was not merely about counting money but protecting the company’s vision, with every department responsible for efficiency and financial sustainability. Mr Barnes reaffirmed Dzata Cement’s ambition to become Ghana’s number-one cement manufacturing company by 2030, saying the first five years had laid the foundation while the next five would build the legacy through disciplined investment, stronger distribution, dependable production, customer service and tighter cost management. The company also intends ultimately to expand into ready-mixed concrete and other cement-related products and services.

Burkina: qui a volé l’identité de Simon Tiemtoré?
items.description: Ceci est un communiqué officiel portant démenti relatif à une publication frauduleuse utilisant l’image et l’identité de Simon Tiemtoré, chairman de Vista Group. «Vista Group porte à la connaissance de l'opinion publique qu'une publication circulant sur les réseaux sociaux et certaines plateformes numériques utilise frauduleusement l'image et l'identité de Monsieur Simon TIEMTORÉ, Chairman du Groupe Bancaire Vista , pour promouvoir une prétendue plateforme d'investissement dénommée «Vigoureux Torlian», promettant des gains financiers de 4 millions de FCFA par mois. Vista Group tient à démentir formellement les informations contenues dans cette publication et à préciser que Monsieur Simon TIEMTORÉ n'a aucun lien avec cette plateforme, ni avec les offres d'investissement qui y sont présentées. Les déclarations qui lui sont attribuées sont totalement infondées et ne sauraient, en aucun cas, engager sa responsabilité ou celle des entités de Vista Group. Face à cette utilisation abusive de l'image et de l'identité de son Chairman, Vista Group condamne fermement ces pratiques frauduleuses susceptibles d'induire le public en erreur et de porter atteinte à la réputation de ses dirigeants et de ses institutions. Le Groupe invite par conséquent les populations, ses clients et l'ensemble de ses partenaires à faire preuve de la plus grande vigilance, à ne donner aucune suite aux sollicitations liées à cette prétendue offre d'investissement et à ne procéder à aucun transfert de fonds. Vista Group rappelle que toute information officielle relative à ses activités et à celles de ses filiales est exclusivement diffusée à travers ses canaux de communication institutionnels. Vista Group se réserve le droit d'engager toute action judiciaire appropriée à l'encontre des auteurs de cette usurpation d'identité et de toute personne impliquée dans la diffusion de ces fausses informations. Vista Group remercie l'ensemble de ses partenaires et le grand public pour leur vigilance et leur confiance. Fait à Ouagadougou, le 8 octobre 2026 La Direction Générale VISTA GROUP NDLR: En rappel, Simon Tiemtoré, l’homme d’affaires burkinabè et patron de Lilium Capital Group, a contribué, aux côtés de Marob Strategies and Consulting DIFC Ltd, à structurer et exécuter un mandat financier global d’un milliard de dollars pour Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals (DPRP), fasant ainsi la fierté du Burkina Faso et de l’Afrique sur l’échiquier financier mondial. Au titre de son appui au mieux-être de ses «frères et sœurs» burkinabè, sur une longue liste d’actions posées, il vient de participer, en tant que chairman du Groupe bancaire Vista à la la première cotation à la Bourse Régionale des Valeurs Mobilières (BRVM), des titres issus de l’opération Diaspora Bonds. C’est encore Simon Tiemtoré, pour ne citer que sa dernière œuvre au profit des familles et enfants burkinabè, a déboursé, en deux ans, une enveloppe de plus de 26,8 millions francs CFA pour accompagner près de 193 élèves orphelins de soldats tombés sur les champs de combat. L’article Burkina: qui a volé l’identité de Simon Tiemtoré? est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: The fallen noble profession: The sad tale of the Ghanaian teacher
items.description: For years, it was a noble profession. To be a teacher was to be respected. Today, it has become an object of ridicule. The Ghanaian teacher, who holds the future of this country in a chalk-stained hand, is now the punchline of jokes in tro-tros, markets, and family gatherings. It is a painful irony that the one who teaches others to become rich is unable to escape poverty himself. It is now described as a profession good for ladies, because the income alone cannot sustain a family. The assumption is that a woman will be supported by her husband, so she can afford to teach. For a man who must be the breadwinner, the salary is an insult. Consequently, many now see teaching not as a career, but as a stepping stone. It is something you do while waiting for a better opportunity. The ultimate disrespect comes from the very children we taught. After nurturing them and watching them graduate and become successful, they meet you on the road and ask with surprise, “Sir, are you still teaching?” As if to remain a teacher is a sign of failure. Walk into any staff common room at the end of the month, and the conversation is the same. It is about OD. Overdraft has become an unofficial part of the teacher’s salary. We are the first to get to the bank on payday, not because we are eager to save, but because our debts are waiting. Among all civil servants, the teacher is known as the poorest. While others are discussing plots of land and investments, the teacher is calculating how to make his salary reach the next month. We have become synonymous with being miserly, not because we love money too much, but because we have too little of it. This economic hardship has created a social stigma that follows us everywhere. Society now defines a teacher by his deprivation. The wearing of second-hand clothes, popularly known as “foos or abroni waa wo”, and used shoes is seen as our hobby. We are mocked for marrying food vendors, as if seeking a partner who can ensure you will at least eat is a crime. These jokes, though laughed at, carry a painful truth about how low the profession has sunk in the eyes of the public. If the situation in public schools is bad, the plight of our colleagues in the private sector is worse. Those teaching in schools run by a single individual or family suffer the most. Their salaries are nothing to write home about, and to make matters worse, the salary for January will be paid in the middle of February. They work the hardest, are supervised the most, yet are paid the least, with no job security and no pension to look forward to. The shame is most felt at home. During family gatherings where contributions are made for funerals or weddings, the teacher is the one who contributes the least. He bows his head in shame while his younger brother, who stopped school in Junior High School and learned a trade, contributes ten times more. It is in these moments that the most painful words are whispered to him: “There were so many lucrative jobs out there, but you chose to become a teacher.” The pride that once came with the profession has been replaced with quiet regret. The reality of our daily lives makes these words even harder to bear. We struggle to pay our rent in Accra and Kumasi, where landlords demand two years’ advance. We find it incredibly difficult to cater for the higher education of our own children, even though we spend our lives educating other people’s children. We go on vacation, but we cannot go on holiday. A trip to Ada or even across the border to Togo is a luxury we cannot afford. Our vacation is spent under a mango tree, marking piles of exercise books with a red pen that is almost dry. And so, we are told our reward is in heaven. This is the final consolation given to us. The white missionaries indeed brought both the Bible and the Western school system. It seems, however, that they left the promise of a heavenly reward for the teacher while others enjoy their earthly rewards. The teacher is told to be content with the knowledge that he is doing God’s work. But even the Bible declares that a worker deserves his wages. This is not a plea for pity. It is a call for national reflection. A nation that mocks its teachers mocks its own future. A hungry teacher cannot effectively teach a hungry child. A teacher who is constantly worried about where his next meal will come from cannot inspire children to dream big. If Ghana wants a quality education system that can compete with the rest of the world, we must first restore dignity to the teaching profession. This goes beyond the annual Best Teacher awards. It requires a living wage that reflects the importance of our work, better conditions of service, and genuine respect from society. Until we do this, we will continue to lose our brightest teachers to other professions, and our classrooms will be left with those who have no other choice. The joke, in the end, will not be on the teacher. It will be on the nation that chose to laugh at the very hands that built it. For without the teacher, there is no doctor, no lawyer, no engineer, and no president.

items.title: Cybersecurity compliance mandatory for critical infrastructure owners – Sam George
items.description: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has stressed that cybersecurity obligations are mandatory for owners of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). Speaking at a workshop on “CII Resilience Beyond IT: Securing Ghana’s Operational Technology Ecosystem”, organised by the Cyber Security Authority (CSA) in partnership with Cybershield as part of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month (NCSAM) 2026, the Minister said compliance with the Directive for the Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure is essential to responsible digital operations and national resilience. He urged CII owners to strengthen cybersecurity governance, appoint accredited cybersecurity leadership and ensure timely reporting of cybersecurity incidents. He also called for regular audits and vulnerability assessments to identify and address weaknesses in critical systems. The Minister further stressed the need for CII owners to engage only Tier 1 licensed cybersecurity service providers, noting that effective protection of Ghana’s critical infrastructure requires sustained compliance and strong cybersecurity practices.

Teachers’ strike: Final-year SHS students worry over lost learning time and WASSCE preparation
items.description: With little or no academic instruction, final-year senior high students are particularly worried about lost learning time as the nationwide teachers’ strike continues. For many students in Kumasi, the school day has become a routine of reporting to class, sitting for hours and eventually returning without a single lesson. The nationwide strike by the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT) and Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) began on September 25, 2026, over outstanding concerns including the placement of promoted teachers on new salary levels and negotiations on conditions of service. Recent engagements between the government and the unions have so far failed to produce a resolution. For students, however, the disagreement between government and teachers has translated into something much more immediate: a growing gap in their education. “We come to school, and there is nothing to do,” said a Form Three student at Prempeh College who described the experience as frustrating, particularly for students preparing to leave secondary school. “We don’t have any work to do. No teachers have been coming to class, and we have little time to cover the syllabus before WASSCE starts,” he added. The student said the normal school routine has continued, but without teachers, much of the day is spent simply waiting. Another Form Three student said the situation was especially worrying for final-year students who have limited time left to prepare academically. According to the student, some learners have resorted to extra classes as the only available avenue for structured teaching, but that option is not accessible to everyone. Students whose families cannot afford additional lessons risk falling further behind, raising concerns about the unequal impact of the strike on learners from different economic backgrounds. For final-year students, the uncertainty is particularly concerning as they prepare for examinations and the transition beyond secondary school. Earlier observations in Accra showed classrooms largely vacant, with some students left on school compounds without teachers to supervise or teach them. In some schools, students were seen playing while others remained in classrooms. The situation has continued to put pressure on school authorities, who must keep students occupied and safe while normal academic activities remain suspended. Amid the disruption, some schools are finding ways to ensure students are not completely idle. One such response has been the organisation of activities under Freshers Week, giving newly admitted students opportunities to participate in programmes designed to keep them engaged during a period when regular teaching has been severely affected. Although such activities cannot replace classroom instruction, they provide students with structured engagement and an opportunity to develop interests outside the traditional academic setting. The activities also offer a degree of relief from what has otherwise become a monotonous routine of coming to school, sitting in classrooms and waiting without lessons. For freshers, the programmes can help with social interaction, orientation and integration into school life, while giving the broader student population something constructive to participate in during the disruption. But students say activities cannot replace teaching. Despite the positives, students acknowledge that such initiatives are not a substitute for their teachers. For students in Form Three, in particular, entertainment and extracurricular activities cannot address the academic pressure created by weeks without regular lessons and can only serve as a temporary relief in this period. Their concern is not simply about being bored. It is about the cumulative effect of lost instructional time. With every additional day without teaching, students worry about topics that remain uncovered, revision schedules that are disrupted and the possibility of having to catch up under intense pressure once teachers eventually return. The government has repeatedly appealed to the unions to suspend the strike, and discussions are still ongoing to get teachers back in the classrooms as soon as possible. For students, the hope is simple: that the negotiations end soon and teachers return to their classrooms. Until then, school authorities are left trying to keep students occupied, while learners — especially those in their final year — continue to count the cost of days without teaching. While Freshers Week and other school activities may provide a welcome distraction, students say what they ultimately need is to get back to learning.

items.title: Hong Kong police arrest students as alleged key figures in HK$2.16 million scam ring
items.description: Hong Kong police have arrested two tertiary students suspected of being key members of a fraud and money-laundering syndicate behind fake job advertisements, dating scams and bogus concert ticket sales. items.title: Los estudiantes de Francia presentan 10 reivindicaciones para detener sus protestas
items.description: Las protestas de los estudiantes franceses continúan y mantienen su intensidad tras varias semanas. París, Marsella, Nantes… Todas las grandes ciudades han visto desfilar otra vez a miles de jóvenes este jueves con pancartas contra el Gobierno y la degradación del sistema público educativo. En París volvió a convocarse una gran marcha en el centro de la ciudad con el apoyo también de otros sectores y de las universidades. Esa es la gran novedad. El movimiento crece mientras el primer ministro, Sébastien Lecornu, no ha logrado apaciguarlo con respuestas tras su estéril comparecencia del miércoles por la noche. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Supremo tumba el decreto del Gobierno para frenar las universidades ‘chiringuito’
items.description: El Tribunal Supremo ha tumbado la modificación del decreto que trata de frenar la creación de nuevas universidades sin calidad que aprobó el Gobierno en octubre pasado para endurecer los criterios. El alto tribunal no ha entrado a debatir el contenido de la norma porque ha concluido que el procedimiento de tramitación urgente que utilizó el Gobierno para aprobar el decreto, saltándose el trámite de consulta pública, no estaba justificado. “Es imposible apreciar alguna circunstancia que conecte la urgencia con el contenido que se pretendía dar a la norma reglamentaria y que debería quedar suficientemente justificado en el Acuerdo del Consejo de Ministros” por el que se aprobó el decreto, señala la sentencia, a la que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS. items.title: Sahara : l’argumentaire juridique autour de l’autonomie appelé à prendre une nouvelle dimension
items.description: Alors que le dossier du Sahara doit être discuté au niveau du Conseil de sécurité au cours du mois d'octobre, et face aux derniers développements, le politologue Mohamed Bouden recommande le renforcement de l'argumentation juridique et politique autour de l’autonomie et de s'appuyer sur la reconnaissance croissante, par certains États, de la pertinence juridique de cette solution. Le dossier du Sahara devrait entrer dans une phase importante les prochains mois après les échéances au niveau du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU. Ce 7 et 8 octobre, deux réunions sont programmées, la première avec les pays contributeurs de la mission d'observation du cessez-le-feu MINURSO, la seconde comprend des consultations à huis clos avec les membres du Conseil avant l'expiration du mandat de la mission le 31 octobre. Mais devant les tentatives de certaines parties de bloquer le processus onusien et de promouvoir des récits fondés sur des interprétations différentes du cadre onusien, ainsi que sur des références historiques et géopolitiques dont la pertinence fait l’objet de contestations, il devient important de remettre au devant de la scène un argumentaire juridique solide, selon Mohamed Bouden. Pour le politologue, l'argument juridique devrait prendre une place croissante au-delà des actions diplomatiques. Cela passe en s’appuyant notamment sur la résolution 2797 de l’ONU et sur la reconnaissance croissante, par certains États, de la pertinence de cette solution. Il défend « d’adopter deux axes argumentatifs complémentaires « , au niveau national, notamment en priorisant l’arsenal normatif que représente la résolution 2797 des Nations unies et de l’impact juridique et politique qu’elle a produit, ainsi qu'en mettant en lumière les avantages de l’autonomie auprès d'Etats influents. Dans un message publié sur Facebook, le politologue, estime que le premier point devrait s’articuler autour de l’arsenal normatif que représente la résolution 2797 des Nations unies et de l’impact juridique et politique qu’elle a produit. Pour rappel, la résolution avait renouvelé le mandat de la MINURSO d'un an, et appelé toutes les parties prenantes à avancer vers une solution politique qui prend pour base la proposition marocaine d’autonomie. Il s'agit également de « la nécessité de faire face aux tentatives de certaines parties de nier cet impact, en cherchant à diluer la bataille autour de son interprétation et à promouvoir des conceptions qui constituent, sans aucun doute, davantage des contraintes que des contributions ». Bouden explique qu'en second lieu, la proposition d'autonomie aurait contribué à établir ce que l’on pourrait qualifier de « doctrine juridique sur l’autonomie au Sahara marocain » . Il recommande de développer davantage les avantages de l’autonomie et la manière dont celle-ci a atteint, auprès d’un certain nombre d’États influents, le niveau de conviction quant à son caractère juridiquement obligatoire, connu dans la doctrine juridique latine sous le terme d’ « opinio juris ». « Il s’agit d’une expression internationale particulière dont la portée dépasse la simple formulation de positions politiques », estime-t-il . Le politologue soutient en outre que « cette doctrine constitue une réalité juridique cohérente, capable de faire face à toute donnée juridique infondée » et qu'elle permettrait de « neutraliser toute manipulation des concepts et d’écarter les récits issus des archives d’un passé lointain ou de contextes géopolitiques éloignés de la réalité locale ». The post Sahara : l’argumentaire juridique autour de l’autonomie appelé à prendre une nouvelle dimension appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: The Bamba revolution and a maiden broadcast
items.description: Last weekend, a long-awaited Kukurudu Delegates Congress ended with a new executive whose names and faces ‘passeth’ all understanding. As expected, this has led to champagne celebrations in places, and fear and panic elsewhere. It’s clearly the type of congress that should have come with an advisory: ‘caution: painkillers advisable ahead of results declaration.’ As it turned out, a few contestants went home blowing their noses in funeral lamentation; and one or two contestants pleading alibi for the swearing-in ceremony due to congress ‘fatigue.’ The rival party, on its part, was asleep with one eye open, and clearly heart-broken; but I respect their firm decision to endure collateral waist pains in dignified silence. At the Congress, the list of candidates offering to serve the elephant party was a virtual who is who, and could have been flag bearer contenders: John Boadu the supremo; JFK, Hawa Koomson, Boakye Agyarko, Mustapha Hamid, Nana Akomea, Nana B, Titus Glover; Miracles Aboagye, Abankwa, Thompson, Dr China, etc.; a solid team of experienced game changers vying to die for their party. But a few other candidates drew giggles and could have been confronted by congress organisers: ‘Krakye, before God and Man, which part of your body qualifies you to be Vice Chairman?’ Such contestants must have lost their way, and strayed to the wrong ‘funeral.’ This was a party of lawyers, indeed an Abrɔfosɛm People’s Party. ‘What do you want here? ’ Of the 11 vacant slots, the position of 1st Vice Chairman was the most sought after: attracting 13 powdered faces. It was the closest to the Supreme Chair position, which attracted only four names, one of whom later took to his heels from stage fright. The 1st Vice is the spot often eyed by high-profile persons who pretend it was all they sought, but in truth use this as a stepping stone to higher heavens. In the absence of the chairman at meetings, the 1st Vice may quietly thank the good lord for his boss’s unfortunate toothache, and unwillingly replace him upstairs, until the missing tooth is providentially restored. Happily, our society permits references to the 1st Vice Chair as simply ‘Chairman Koo Hia,’ since ‘Vice Chairman Koo Hia’ is rather a mouthful. At the congress, the category of 1st Vice Chairman presented several known dignitaries, plus one anonymous soul who in public functions would normally attract the label, ‘et cetera et cetera,’ in the words of the MC. Did ‘Mr Et cetera’ lose his way, jay-walking to a NPP Congress? No. He was Kojo Bamba, a former bodyguard of charismatic Nana B, who was also in the race. Was it then a contest between Master and Servant? Would Bamba not rather bow out in deference? No. The servant’s campaign message indeed was a celebration of Asante diplomacy at its best: ‘Fellow party members, with due respect, please go ahead and vote for the two learned gentlemen (akrakyefo): Nana B and Nana Akomea. But simply add my name as the third in your order of preference. I am a mere security hand, and will be in attendance to protect the ballot if added; my duty will be to simply stop the rival party from bullying and intimidating us.’ This was not a campaign of boss abuse, insult, vilification among competing kinsmen. It was a fragment of Asante diplomacy dating back to the 19th century. At the weekend Congress, Bamba looked different among contestants. He was in military gear, depicting the look of the Burkinabe capo, Captain Ibrahim Traore, followed by teeming throngs of youth. Dressed in military gear, Bamba’s appearance alone spoke louder than words. What was unknown was Bamba’s widespread popularity among delegates at the Congress: accomplices with sealed lips. The long and weary day and night ended with a results declaration at dawn, which kept trickling in until the bombshell. While most results conformed to wide expectations, the breaking news swiveled around Kojo Bamba, the faceless wretch who had shattered expectations and won the enviable slot of 1st Vice Chairman. He had humbled his superiors, whacking them to Second and Third Positions. This was a historic revolt by the grassroots, and a major landmark in our political history. The optics were shattering, and led to a courteous alibi at the swearing-in ceremony, where the two Big Men were unavoidably absent due to ‘fatigue.’ The casualty ward quickly filled to capacity, but has since thinned out. Like true democrats, many have conveyed congratulations to Chairman Boadu and others, including Kojo Bamba, the new hero. Quietly disturbed is the rival Umbrella party, currently nail biting, and contemplating a 24-hour retreat. Conference Theme? The Bamba Factor in Ghana’s democracy. Below, I humbly reproduce excerpts of ‘Chairman Bamba’s maiden broadcast to his teeming fans last weekend: Chairman Bamba speaks: “I come here today armed with profuse thanks. I cannot rise to leadership leaving my own people behind. Colleagues, please lace your boots for the task ahead…When i was doing my rounds during the campaign, I pleaded with you to vote for me to win. My promise was to hand over power back to you. During voting at the Congress, you neither gave me the third nor the second position as Vice Chairman; you honored me with the position of 1st Vice Chairman. It is now my duty to give back the power to you, but also add several more parliamentary seats to our party. That’s my job description. “I will make sure the new national leadership of NPP comes down to your level. Our new leadership has individuals with varying backgrounds. It is often said that the NPP cannot be led by people who are not lawyers, who are without master’s degree or professorial titles. I will prove them wrong… Politics is not won with certificates but with humility, self-sacrifice…commitment and courage. I will be guided by these virtues to prove others wrong. You can be a leader if you are human with blood circulating in you; if you have a tongue to speak and ears to listen. You can even aim to be president: it is neither by riches nor poverty. Those of you who were misled to follow another political party because they embraced all, including grassroots; today, your own brother is here. Please file behind me, and lend me your support. “Tro tro drivers, auto mechanics, carpenters, your own is now here. When you want to visit me, there is no need to write an application; no need to book an appointment…my office is yours.… Come help me bring back the NPP. Are you not proud your own man comes next after Mahmoud Bawumia and John Boadu? Are you not proud? Together we can even exceed the achievements of our forebears. “I who am undeserving… I who was taken for nothing in a party full of lawyers and doctors, full of professors; a party reserved for people with multiple degrees. A party not cut for senior high school graduates… You would normally not find me here. But today, the party has rewarded the servant working under his master; it has rewarded a mere tenant, a mere security guard…If the party has rewarded me, Kojo Bamba, a poor underdog… if it has uplifted a virtual homeless, let no one belittle themselves… Based on your hard work for the party, you will be rewarded. Help me to succeed so it may not be said, ‘we told you, those holding no degrees or masters; non-PhDs, non-lawyers, non-medical doctors cannot lead the NPP.’ I will do all I can with your help to prove sceptics wrong. “Your NPP party does not discriminate against the rich or poor, literate or non-literate, or those with or without academic certificates. Note that I am not beyond advice. Feel free to come and advise me when I return from break; so I will be well equipped to contribute my quota working for DMB. I am a Ghetto Boy; your own is now here… Gone are the days when we worked tirelessly for others to enjoy. My father once told me, ‘He who has pounded the food to make a pleasant meal cannot be stopped from dipping his hands…’ “Today, I virtually panic waking up to see where I am: a mere underdog.”

items.title: Déficience mentale : en Côte d’Ivoire, un refuge à vie contre le rejet de la société
items.description: À la fin des grandes vacances, Ahou Albertine Kouadio a ramené son fils Alexandre dans un centre accueillant à vie des personnes atteintes de déficience mentale. Un lieu sûr, à l'abri du rejet et des violences qui frappent ceux que l'on traite parfois de « sorciers » en Côte d'Ivoire. Plus de 80 millions de personnes vivent avec un handicap en Afrique selon l'ONU, qui déplore un cruel manque d'actions pour leur intégration. Créé en janvier, le Réseau africain pour l'inclusion des personnes handicapées (RAIPH), une initiative pour l'instant présente dans 17 pays, a d'ailleurs récemment qualifié le manque de prise en charge du handicap d' »urgence continentale ». À l'Arche, située à Bouaké (centre), deuxième ville de Côte d'Ivoire, les personnes accueillies sont âgées de 8 à 60 ans et portent différents handicaps intellectuels. Trente-et-une vivent actuellement sur place et près de 100 viennent régulièrement participer à des activités. La structure, qui fait partie d'une fédération d'associations présente dans 38 pays, est l'un des rares centres spécialisés dans le handicap mental et l'un des plus importants de Côte d'Ivoire par sa capacité d'accueil, à vie, de dizaines de personnes, depuis 1974. Alexandre, « je l'ai aimé beaucoup plus que mes autres enfants », confie à l'AFP d'une voix douce Ahou Albertine Kouadio, 70 ans. Le placer ici, depuis plusieurs années, « c'est difficile, mais je lutte », ajoute-t-elle. Car sa présence à la maison pourrait être source d'inquiétudes. En Côte d'Ivoire, comme dans d'autres pays africains, les enfants porteurs d'un handicap, quel qu'il soit, sont souvent rejetés, qualifiés de « sorciers » ou d' »enfants serpents », pour ceux qui se meuvent difficilement. Et le pays compte très peu de structures publiques de santé dédiées aux personnes atteintes de déficience intellectuelle, souvent envoyées dans des retraites religieuses non conventionnelles pour être « soignées ». Dans des cas extrêmes, elles sont « accompagnées », c'est-à-dire tuées par leurs proches ou des gens de la communauté, souvent par empoisonnement ou par noyade, rapporte le directeur du centre, Célestin N'Goran. – « Beaucoup de préjugés » – « Je suis heureuse quand il est ici », dit Mme Kouadio au sujet de son fils en racontant ses inquiétantes fugues nocturnes et le risque de mauvaises rencontres. Assis à ses côtés, Alexandre, bientôt 30 ans, peine à s'exprimer par les mots mais affiche de larges sourires. Odette, plus âgée, dont le prénom a été modifié pour préserver son anonymat, a rejoint le centre dès l'enfance. Ses parents sont décédés et elle n'a plus de famille pour lui rendre visite. Lorsqu'elle erre dans la cour, elle répète inlassablement le nom de son village. Certains enfants sont déposés ici très jeunes et n'ont plus aucune nouvelle de leurs proches. « Les enfants ne sont pas des sorciers, mais ce sont des personnes à part entière qui ont droit à la vie, nous devons respecter leur dignité et les intégrer dans la société », plaide Célestin N'Goran. Les personnes accueillies à l'Arche, dont la plupart sont sous traitement neuroleptique, participent à diverses activités : apprentissage de l'alphabet, coloriage ou maraîchage. Le centre effectue également un suivi régulier dans les familles, pour voir « si ces enfants, à la maison, arrivent à suivre ce que nous leur apprenons ici », ajoute Marine Tardy Kouamé, assistante sociale. Elle amène aussi les parents à « accepter leurs enfants tels qu'ils sont », par des actions de sensibilisation et des groupes de parole. « Le handicap intellectuel est peu connu, ce qui fait qu'il y a beaucoup de préjugés », déplore Célestin N'Goran. Il est « en marge » par rapport aux autres handicaps, moteurs ou sensoriels, estime-t-il. Dans une tribune publiée en juillet par le média français spécialisé Handinova, la nouvelle initiative africaine RAIPH évoque des « avancées normatives indéniables » sur le continent, mais liste de nombreuses difficultés. Notamment « une réalité encore mal documentée », un « déficit de formation des personnels soignants », « une faible intégration » du sujet « dans les politiques sanitaires nationales » et des « représentations sociales tenaces ». AFP

items.title: Plan RELANCE : Le Burkina Faso veut mobiliser 36 000 milliards FCFA d’ici 2030
items.description: Le Burkina Faso entend franchir une nouvelle étape dans sa transformation économique avec le Plan RELANCE sur la période 2026-2030. Présenté par le ministre de l'Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, le mercredi 7 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou dans le cadre de l'exposition gouvernementale se déroulant au Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), le programme prévoit la mobilisation de plus de 36 000 milliards de FCFA sur cinq ans, dont près des deux tiers devraient provenir des ressources propres de l'État. Après quatre années consacrées à la consolidation des finances publiques, à la mobilisation des ressources et à la mise en place de nouveaux instruments économiques, le gouvernement burkinabè veut désormais « changer d'échelle ». C'est l'ambition affichée à travers le Plan RELANCE 2026-2030, présenté par le ministre de l'Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, dans le cadre de l'initiative « Dialogue avec le peuple », à l'occasion de la phase 2 de la 3e édition des Journées d'engagement patriotique et participation citoyenne (JEPPC). « Nous avons consolidé. Nous avons réformé. Nous avons créé des instruments. Il nous faut maintenant changer d’échelle », a déclaré le ministre. Plus de 36 000 milliards de FCFA à mobiliser Le Plan RELANCE prévoit la mobilisation de plus de 36 000 milliards de FCFA sur la période 2026-2030. Près des deux tiers de ce financement devront provenir des ressources propres de l'État Burkinabè. Pour le ministre Nacanabo, cette orientation traduit la volonté de construire un modèle de développement davantage fondé sur les capacités internes du pays. « Nous voulons construire un développement dont le moteur principal se trouve chez nous », a-t-il affirmé. Sur cette enveloppe globale, plus de 12 000 milliards de FCFA d'investissements structurants sont annoncés, notamment dans les infrastructures, l'énergie, l’industrialisation, l’agriculture, le numérique et le développement du capital humain. Une croissance moyenne de 7,2 % visée Le gouvernement ambitionne, à travers ce plan, d'atteindre une croissance économique moyenne de 7,2 % par an. Toujours selon le Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo, le Plan RELANCE vise également une progression des exportations de plus de 10 % par an, le renforcement de l'industrie manufacturière, l'accélération de la souveraineté alimentaire et énergétique ainsi qu'une réduction significative de la pauvreté. Derrière ces objectifs macroéconomiques, le MEF veut mettre en évidence des réalisations concrètes pour les populations. « Derrière les 36 000 milliards, il faut voir autre chose : des barrages, des routes, de l'électricité, des industries, des exploitations agricoles modernes, des écoles, des hôpitaux, des emplois, des entrepreneurs », a expliqué Dr Aboubakar Nacanabo. Quatre piliers pour transformer l'économie Le Plan RELANCE 2026-2030 repose sur quatre piliers majeurs. Il s'agit de la consolidation de la sécurité et de la cohésion sociale, de la refondation de l'État et de la gouvernance, du développement du capital humain et de la transformation durable de l'économie à travers des infrastructures modernes et des investissements productifs. Cette approche doit permettre, selon le ministre, de faire évoluer le Burkina Faso d’une logique de gestion des contraintes vers une dynamique de création de richesse et de prospérité. « Notre ambition ne doit pas être seulement de mieux gérer la pauvreté. Notre ambition doit être de créer la prospérité », a-t-il lancé. Le financement du plan repose largement sur la capacité du Burkina Faso à mobiliser ses propres ressources. Cette orientation s'inscrit dans la dynamique présentée par le ministère depuis 2022, avec l'augmentation des recettes publiques, la mobilisation sur le marché financier régional, le Fonds de soutien patriotique et la mise en place de nouveaux instruments financiers. Pour Aboubakar Nacanabo, la souveraineté économique passe nécessairement par la capacité du pays à financer une part croissante de ses propres ambitions. « La souveraineté économique ne se proclame pas. Elle se finance. Elle ne se décrète pas. Elle se produit. Elle ne s'importe pas. Elle se construit », a-t-il déclaré. De ce fait, le ministre appelle ainsi les producteurs, entrepreneurs, investisseurs, travailleurs, fonctionnaires, jeunes, chercheurs et membres de la diaspora à prendre part à cette nouvelle phase de transformation. « Maintenant que nous savons que nous pouvons avancer, nous devons accélérer » De l'avis du MEF, les résultats obtenus depuis 2022 constituent moins un aboutissement qu'un point d'appui pour la prochaine étape. « Nous n'avons pas encore atteint notre destination. Nous avons simplement démontré que nous sommes capables d'avancer. Et maintenant que nous savons que nous pouvons avancer, nous devons accélérer », a-t-il soutenu. Avec le Plan RELANCE 2026-2030, le gouvernement entend donc faire de la mobilisation des ressources, de l'investissement productif et de la transformation locale les moteurs d'une nouvelle dynamique économique. L'objectif affiché est clair bâtir un Burkina Faso « souverain, productif, prospère et respecté ». Jean-François SOME Minute.bf

items.title: Canadian writer Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
items.description: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the award-giving body said on Thursday. The prize is awarded by the Swedish Academy and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2m). Canadian poet and essayist Carson’s work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix. She is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influences her work which ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse novels such as Autobiography of Red from 1998. Her style is exemplified in Norma Jeane Baker of Troy from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides’ play Helen and Marilyn Monroe. Carson takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award, which often divides opinion among book lovers. The Academy has been lambasted for ignoring some of the literary titans of the last 120 years such as Leo Tolstoy, Virginia Woolf and Jorge Luis Borges, criticised for snubbing US authors, though it gave the prize to singer-songwriter Bob Dylan in 2016, and accused of being too obscure in its choices. Defenders say the Academy has made popular picks, such as Colombia’s Gabriel Garcia Marquez in 1982 and Doris Lessing in 2007, arguing that part of its task is to highlight lesser-known literary traditions and encourage readers to broaden their horizons. Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes for achievements in literature, science and peace have been awarded since 1901. Last year’s prize was won by Hungarian writer Laszlo Krasznahorkai , dubbed the “master of the apocalypse” by American critic Susan Sontag.

items.title: Finale CAN 2025 : le TAS entame l’examen du dossier, la décision ne sera pas immédiate
items.description: La séance d’audition consacrée au litige opposant le Maroc, le Sénégal et la CAF s’est ouverte ce jeudi à Lausanne. Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) ne devrait pas rendre sa décision dans l’immédiat. Le dossier opposant le Maroc au Sénégal et à la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) est entré ce jeudi dans une nouvelle phase. L’audience devant le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a débuté à Lausanne, en Suisse, en présence des représentants des différentes parties. Selon Mathieu Reeb, directeur général du TAS, les parties sont représentées par leurs avocats et la séance se déroule conformément au calendrier établi au préalable entre les conseils. Les plaidoiries doivent se poursuivre jusqu’à 15h ou 15h30, avec une possible prolongation jusqu’à 16h au maximum. Une organisation qui traduit le cadre strict fixé pour l’examen de ce dossier, engagé depuis plusieurs mois. Trois arbitres pour examiner le litige Le dossier est examiné par une formation arbitrale composée de trois membres. Elle est présidée par le Français Gérald Simon, assisté de l’Allemand Ulrich Haas et de l’Italien Luigi Fumagalli. Cette formation devra prendre connaissance des arguments présentés par les différentes parties avant de délibérer sur le fond du litige. Le directeur général du TAS a indiqué que la juridiction sportive souhaitait parvenir à une décision dans les meilleurs délais après la clôture de l’audience. Un point important reste toutefois à préciser : aucune décision n’est attendue ce jeudi, ni vendredi, selon Mathieu Reeb. Quelques jours ou plusieurs semaines d’attente Le délai dépendra du temps nécessaire aux trois arbitres pour examiner les éléments du dossier et arrêter leur position. Mathieu Reeb évoque une décision qui pourrait intervenir dans quelques jours comme dans plusieurs semaines. Le TAS ne fixe donc, à ce stade, aucune date précise pour l’annonce de sa décision. Le responsable de la juridiction arbitrale a également laissé entendre que de nouveaux éléments pourraient être communiqués dans l’après-midi, permettant d’en savoir davantage sur le déroulement de l’audience et sur les prochaines étapes de la procédure. Après plusieurs mois de procédure, le dossier entre ainsi dans sa dernière ligne droite. Mais malgré l’ouverture de l’audience ce jeudi à Lausanne, les différentes parties devront encore patienter avant de connaître la position définitive du TAS. items.title: Semaines décisives pour les quotas de capture des crevettes rouges par les pêcheurs tunisiens
items.description: Des semaines décisives s’annoncent pour la filière halieutique tunisienne dans ses relations avec l’Union européenne (UE). Du 26 au 30 octobre 2026, la Tunisie participera à Rome à la 49 e session de la Commission générale des pêches pour la Méditerranée (CGPM), chargée de définir de nouvelles mesures de gestion des stocks et de contrôles européens des quotas de crevettes rouges. Parallèlement, une délégation de l’UE est attendue en Tunisie le 16 novembre prochain; en prévision de cette visite, les contrôles et les travaux ont été intensifiés dans les ports de pêche de Sousse et de Hergla. Le premier dossier concerne la crevette rouge dans le canal de Sicile. La recommandation CGPM/48/2025/9 a prorogé pour 2026 la période transitoire du plan pluriannuel de gestion dans les sous-zones 12 à 16, réduisant de 3 % les limites de capture pour la crevette rouge géante ( Aristaeomorpha foliacea ) et la crevette violette ( Aristeus antennatus ). Les captures tunisiennes en question Pour la Tunisie, la limite fixée pour 2026 concernant la crevette rouge géante est de 36 000 kilogrammes. Selon une note d’information du ministère italien de l’Agriculture, le quota était déjà épuisé le 15 mai, alors que les certificats de capture tunisiens enregistrés sur la plateforme européenne Catch atteignaient par la suite un total d’au moins 50 960 kilogrammes, soit 41,5 % au-delà du plafond autorisé. Le ministère italien (Masaf) a donc appelé les opérateurs italiens à ne pas accepter de lots issus de captures dépassant la limite internationale. Les échanges se poursuivront également sur le plan scientifique. Une réunion technique consacrée à la préparation des données sur la crevette rouge de profondeur en Méditerranée centre-orientale est prévue du 9 au 11 novembre au siège de la FAO à Rome ; elle sera suivie, du 11 au 14 novembre, d’une réunion sur les stocks de Méditerranée centrale. Le volet sanitaire constitue un autre dossier important, distinct de celui des quotas mais crucial pour l’accès au marché européen. Selon Diwan FM, citant Samir Mhiri (responsable de la production animale au Commissariat régional au développement agricole de Sousse), une délégation de l’UE est attendue en Tunisie le 16 novembre. En amont de cette visite, les inspections dans les ports de Sousse et de Hergla ont été intensifiées afin de vérifier les conditions d’hygiène et de salubrité, ainsi que l’état des marchés de gros et des équipements. À Sousse, des travaux sont en phase d’achèvement concernant les sols, le système d’évacuation des eaux usées, les chambres froides et l’installation de production de glace alimentaire. A Hergla, le marché a repris son activité, mais la procédure d’agrément vétérinaire reste à finaliser. Ces interventions s’inscrivent dans le cadre d’une mise aux normes plus large de la filière tunisienne, conformément aux exigences sanitaires applicables aux produits destinés à l’exportation. L’Italie, principal débouche des produits de pêche tunisiens Les enjeux économiques sont considérables. Au cours des sept premiers mois de 2026, la Tunisie a exporté 18 400 tonnes de produits de la pêche pour une valeur de 422,3 millions de dinars (127 millions d'euros). L’Italie demeure le principal débouché, absorbant 34 % des exportations, suivie de l’Espagne avec 12 % ; ensemble, ces deux pays représentent 46 % des exportations tunisiennes de produits de la pêche. Ces deux dossiers restent toutefois distincts : le différend concernant la crevette rouge porte sur les quotas de pêche, la durabilité des stocks et la traçabilité via le système Catch, tandis que la visite en Tunisie du 16 novembre concerne, selon les informations disponibles à ce jour, la conformité sanitaire et vétérinaire de la filière. Tous deux ont néanmoins une incidence sur la capacité de la Tunisie à maintenir un accès régulier de ses produits de la pêche au marché européen. D’après Ansa . L’article Semaines décisives pour les quotas de capture des crevettes rouges par les pêcheurs tunisiens est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Classement FIFA : l’Algérie gagne une place
items.description: Après une victoire contre la Zambie (3-1), un nul face au Burundi (2-2) en éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 et un succès devant le Niger en amical (2-1), , l’équipe d’Algérie gagne une place au classement FIFA publié ce jeudi 8 octobre. Les Fennecs de Brahim Hemdani pointent à la 28 e position au classement général de l’instance du football mondial, contre la 29 e place dans le précédent classement. Classement FIFA : l’Algérie à la 4 e place en Afrique En Afrique, l’Algérie reste dans le top 5 des meilleures sélections, derrière le Maroc (7 e ) qui a perdu une place, le Sénégal (18 e ), l’Égypte (25 e , -1) et devant la Côte d’Ivoire (29 e , +2) et le Nigéria (30 e , -4). Après une Coupe du monde 2026 catastrophique, la Tunisie qui a perdu quatre places pointe à la 61 e position. Pour la tête du classement mondial, l’Espagne, championne du monde en titre, l’Argentine, vice-championne du monde, et la France occupent les trois premières places devant l’Angleterre (4 e ), le Portugal (5 e ), le Brésil (6 e ), le Maroc (7 e ), la Belgique (8 e ), les Pays-Bas (9 e ) et le Mexique (10 e ). items.title: How the Polls Could Be Wrong Again
items.description: Less than a month out from Election Day, the polls are predicting a Democratic rout. According to the election forecaster Nate Silver’s polling average , Democratic Senate candidates are leading in Kansas, which voted for Donald Trump by 16 percentage points in 2024, as well as Alaska, Iowa, Ohio, and Texas, all of which Trump won by more than 10 points. In the House, Democrats are poised to win their largest majority in 18 years. So the polls tell us. Can they be believed? Ever since underestimating Trump in 2016, pollsters have been busy trying to regain the public’s trust, tweaking their methodologies in ways both dramatic and subtle. Perhaps they’ve finally got it right. They seem to think so. “I’m confident that not just ourselves, but the industry, has good technique, good methodology, and that they are reflecting and representing public opinion,” Spencer Kimball, the director of polling at Emerson College, told me. But the industry has been confident before, only to be proved wrong. After 2016, pollsters concluded that they had failed to pay enough attention to educational polarization, the somewhat-new phenomenon of college-educated voters having political preferences that were sharply different from those of voters without a degree. Going forward, the industry would try to include more non-college-educated voters in surveys or, if that proved impossible, would weight those voters’ responses to align with their share of the electorate. In 2018, the pollsters nailed the midterms with little error, suggesting that their adaptations had paid off. Then came 2020. Although the polls correctly gauged that most people preferred Joe Biden to Trump, they underestimated Trump’s support by even more than they did in 2016, especially at the state level. The most memorable example was Wisconsin, where polls had Biden winning by up to 10 percentage points. He wound up winning by less than one. These results left pollsters even more perplexed. If controlling for education didn’t work, what would? Perhaps, they figured, Trump supporters were just different from other voters: less likely to talk to pollsters than other demographically similar voters were. This phenomenon, known as partisan-nonresponse bias, would help explain why midterm polls in the Trump era have generally been more accurate than presidential-election polls: The midterm electorate skews toward politically engaged voters who are more trusting of institutions and more likely to have answered polls. Moving forward, pollsters decided to reach for the bluntest object they had access to: “recalled vote.” If Trump supporters were systematically different, perhaps the best solution was just to ask, “Did you vote for Trump last time?” and then weight the sample so that it had the same Trump-voting percentage as the previous presidential election. When 2022 rolled around, the pollsters once again nailed the midterm. But the recalled-vote tweak didn’t solve the problem in 2024, when polls underestimated Trump by about 3 percent, just as they had in 2016 . In presidential years, at least, nonresponse bias had proved to be extremely difficult to correct for. Even among people who said they had voted for Trump, pollsters could seem to find only the ones who were most likely to vote for a Democrat. [ Marc Novicoff: Gas prices could cost Republicans the midterms ] “At some level, the respondents need to cooperate,” Patrick Ruffini, a Republican pollster, told me. “The individuals that you’re getting on the phone are the wrong people.” Robert Cahaly, the Republican pollster behind the Trafalgar Group, told me, “I’ve found that Republicans tend to be a little more concerned about: Is my name going to be on a list? They want to know, Who are you getting this information for? ” To deal with such an intractable problem, pollsters are resorting to ever more complex solutions. Douglas Rivers, the chief scientist at YouGov, told me that his team is now doing precinct-level modeling, making sure it has not just enough people who say they voted for Trump but also enough people who say they voted for Trump and live in neighborhoods that for the most part voted for Trump. The New York Times and Siena College have invented two new techniques for their jointly conducted polls, “support score” and “energy balancing,” which sound like healing crystals but are in fact statistical weights. They’re used to adjust survey data based on such factors as how Republican a respondent’s name sounds, what car they drive, and how many people in the electorate are demographically identical to them (as in, not just fellow Latinos but fellow young, Latino, agnostic conservatives who live in the suburbs). Even if they manage to correct for nonresponse bias, pollsters have to nail the turnout model. Accurately predicting who’s voting for whom requires figuring out who’s voting at all. Turnout models can swing the results massively. For example, a September YouGov poll had Democrats leading by six percentage points in the U.S. House popular vote, enough for them to narrowly retake the lower chamber. But that was among registered voters. Among respondents whom YouGov deemed to be likely voters, the poll had Democrats winning by 16 points, an outcome that would likely usher in the largest Democratic majority in the House since the 1970s. Even Rivers, who runs YouGov’s American polling outfit, admits that that result is hard to believe. In a recent blog post, he wrote that it “comes from a mix of assumptions that all push the result in Democrats’ favor and that should probably be discounted.” (A newer YouGov poll published yesterday suggests a 10-to-12-point lead among likely voters, depending on the definition of likely .) Turnout models involve a fair amount of informed guessing. Within the general population, the number of Black or white or Asian adults in America is knowable, and pollsters can thus make their samples representative in that sense. But predicting how any of those groups will turn out is always a judgment call. If turnout among certain groups winds up being much lower or much higher than the pollsters predict, that can increase the final error. Democrats—and the polling industry—have a reason to be optimistic about 2026: It’s another midterm in which Trump is not on the ballot and the least engaged voters can be expected to stay home. That’s the kind of election that pollsters have recently gotten right. Then again, the sample size of Trump-era elections—two midterms and three presidential elections—is tiny. Voter behavior sometimes changes in unpredictable ways. And to whatever degree possible, Trump has managed to put himself on the ballot: hand-selecting most of the nominees, barnstorming the country, using taxpayer money to pay for political ads, and forcing his party to host a Trump-centric “midterm convention.” A systematic polling error on the level of 2016 or 2024 would mean that Democrats fall short of Senate control. If the polls overestimate their chances by exactly three points in every state, then Democrats will barely win Alaska, Texas, Michigan, and Ohio, but they won’t pick up Kansas or Iowa or Maine, and they’ll lose Minnesota. The Senate would then be 50–50, Vice President Vance would be the tiebreaker, and dreams of a Democratic Senate would stay dreams. A 2020-level miss would be even worse for Democrats: They’d gain no Senate seats at all on net. Democrats would still take back the House, but much more narrowly. Of course, these are hypotheticals. In reality, whatever polling errors materialize will vary from state to state. And if we could say in advance exactly how they’d vary, we wouldn’t need polls in the first place.

items.title: Milieu carcéral : 17 000 mineurs pris en charge chaque année
items.description: 17.000 mineurs en conflit avec la loi et de jeunes majeurs de moins de 21 ans en danger ont été pris en charge par la Direction générale de la Protection judiciaire et sociale (Dgpjs). Me Moussa Sarr, ministre de la Justice, a fait cette révélation, hier, à l’ouverture du Panel de haut niveau sur la mise en place d’un dispositif et d’un fonds opérants d’insertion et de réinsertion des jeunes en danger ou en conflit avec la loi. Chaque année, la Direction générale de la Protection judiciaire et sociale (Dgpjs) prend en charge 17.000 mineurs, notamment des mineurs en conflit avec la loi, ainsi que de jeunes majeurs de moins de 21 ans en danger. En 2025, 412 pensionnaires des centres de la Dgpjs ont réussi aux examens professionnels. Il s’agit, à en croire le ministre, de 311 attestés et de 101 admis au Certificat d’aptitude professionnelle (Cap) notamment en menuiserie, coiffure, tapisserie, électricité, froid et climatisation et restauration. Cependant, malgré leur diplôme, ces jeunes se heurtent à de nombreuses difficultés. Non seulement ils ne sont pas suffisamment accompagnés pour se perfectionner, mais ils n’ont ni stage d’apprentissage, ni accès à un emploi salarié ou à un microcrédit. 412 pensionnaires reçus aux examens professionnels « Nous leur avons appris un métier et nous les laissons au seuil de l’atelier sans la clé. Or, pour une jeune fille victime de violences comme pour un garçon en danger ou en conflit avec la loi, l’autonomie économique est la meilleure protection contre le retour à la rue, à l’exploitation, à la précarité, parfois à la récidive », a relevé le ministre de la Justice, Me Moussa Sarr. Il présidait, hier, un panel de haut niveau consacré à la mise en place d’un dispositif et d’un fonds opérants d’insertion et de réinsertion des jeunes en danger ou en conflit avec la loi. Dans son discours, il a rappelé que l’État a institué le Fonds de réinsertion des mineurs et jeunes majeurs en situation de vulnérabilité. Mais, précise-t-il, « un fonds seul ne suffit pas ». À en croire Me Sarr, la réussite d’une politique de réinsertion repose sur une mobilisation collective. La réinsertion est une œuvre nationale. Elle exige la solidarité des institutions, l’engagement des entreprises et la confiance de la société civile. Elle exige que chacun prenne sa part de responsabilité. « Les structures publiques doivent inclure cette catégorie de jeunes dans leurs cibles prioritaires par l’octroi de bourses, l’instauration de quotas », a soutenu le ministre, appelant, dans le même sillage, les entreprises à ouvrir leurs portes aux stages, aux contrats de qualification et aux premiers emplois. « Elles doivent voir dans ces jeunes non pas des risques, mais des opportunités », a déclaré le ministre de la Justice. Estimant que ce panel constitue une étape décisive, le ministre indique qu’il doit permettre de bâtir une architecture cohérente reliant protection, rééducation et réinsertion. À cet effet, Me Moussa Sarr a invité les participants à travailler « avec rigueur et créativité à dépasser les cloisonnements institutionnels, à unir vos forces pour que chaque jeune accompagné vers l’autonomie devienne une victoire collective ». Il a, par ailleurs, réaffirmé la détermination du Gouvernement à ne laisser aucun jeune au bord du chemin. Aliou DIOUF
